c3730fb4a41cea69: BIRMINGHAM, Oct 15 — Aston Villa recorded their biggest ever European victory as Nicolas Jackson inspired a 6-0 rout of Fenerbahce in the Champions League yesterday.
Unai Emery’s side won at Villa Park for the first time this season to maintain their 100 percent start in Europe’s elite club competition.
Swiss forward Johan Manzambi put Villa in front and Jackson was on target twice before the interval.
Ross Barkley’s second-half double and Tammy Abraham’s late strike put the seal on a welcome success on home turf for Villa.
Villa Park’s North Stand is currently closed for building work as the club increases the stadium’s capacity to over 50,000.
Amid suggestions that the reduced crowd and lack of noise was affecting Villa’s players, Emery had said there were “no excuses” for failing to win any of their previous three home games.
Languishing in 16th place in the Premier League, Villa responded to Emery’s demand for a more intense performance as they extended their unbeaten run to four games in all competitions.
“Overall it was a very good match. There are still things to improve. It was a strong result for us,” Emery said.
“Keep going forward. It helps confidence for us. We did some changes to get other players confidence and minutes. What we did today was fantastic. The Champions League is very difficult.”
Following a summer of upheaval featuring the sales of star players including Ollie Watkins and Ezri Konsa, the Europa League holders are finally emerging from a turbulent period.
Saluting Jackson’s contribution, Emery added: “He has power to get in behind. He can drop and help as well.
“We need him always to be in the box when we’re attacking. Jackson is our striker.”
Unstoppable Jackson
Villa captain John McGinn fired narrowly wide and Ibrahim Mbaye tested Ederson with a long-range blast in a frenetic opening.
Villa were rewarded for their early barrage in the 12th minute.
Matteo Guendouzi’s wayward header fell to Manzambi, who took a touch before unloading a powerful shot that took a deflection off Milan Skriniar as it whistled past the wrong-footed Ederson.
Manzambi, 21, is the second player to score on his Champions League debut on his birthday.
Jackson’s low strike was pushed away by Ederson, but the Senegal striker wasn’t to be denied.
After Fenerbahce surrendered possession carelessly in the 31st minute, Boubacar Kamara’s pass found Jackson on the edge of the area and he guided a fine finish past Ederson.
Jackson was proving unstoppable and the 25-year-old made it three after 39 minutes.
Taking aim from 18 yards, Jackson’s low drive carried too much power for Ederson, who could only parry it into the net.
It was Jackson’s fifth goal in eight games since arriving from Chelsea in August.
Villa also scored three times in the first half when they won at Club Brugge in their opening game of the Champions League group phase.
Playing his first match in England for four years following his troubled spell at Manchester United, Fenerbahce forward Mason Greenwood was booed mercilessly by Villa fans.
In between the taunts, they were able to celebrate two more goals in the second half.
Barkley slotted home from the penalty spot after Ismail Yuksek fouled Manzambi.
And Barkley struck again four minutes later, meeting Mbaye’s cross with a shot that deflected in off Bartug Elmaz.
Abraham came off the bench to wrap up Villa’s record win as he tapped in Alysson’s cross in stoppage time. — AFP
88f02542dd39f866: LINZ, Oct 15 — Andoni Iraola believes Bradley Barcola’s hat-trick in Liverpool’s 6-3 Champions League win over LASK yesterday will herald the start of a dominant spell for the France forward.
Barcola had come under fire for some lacklustre performances since his blockbuster £123 million (US$161 million) move from Paris Saint-Germain in August.
But he finally started to live up to his hefty price tag with his first goals for Liverpool in his seventh appearance.
Barcola struck twice before the interval at the Raiffeisen Arena after Ronald Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the first half with his maiden goal for the club.
Jeremie Frimpong netted the fourth after the break against the Austrian champions before Barcola completed his treble.

There was still time for Lewis Koumas to score his first Champions League goal as Liverpool maintained their 100 percent record in this season’s tournament after beating Atletico Madrid in their opening game.
“I’m really happy for Bradley because you were asking me yesterday about him not making the numbers, also Florian (Wirtz),” Iraola told reporters on Wednesday.
“I think both of them today played really well. I think they made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick, I think he was a threat always - one-v-one, threatening in behind.
“Also Flo helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I’m happy for both of them.

“I think their confidence, for sure, is very good. I think they feel that we trust them a lot. But at the end, to enjoy a little bit playing in the Champions League away, I think it’s going to be very good for them.”
Barcola won the Champions League with PSG in each of the last two seasons and arrived at Anfield with high expectations.
Iraola is confident his forward’s adaptation to English football will be aided by his goal-spree in Austria.
“Obviously I think he has to enjoy this because to score a hat-trick in the Champions League is always very difficult,” he said.

“Even training yesterday, I could feel he was very lively, sometimes you feel these things. You never know how he’s going to play the next day, but it wasn’t like a big surprise because we were feeling he was in a good place for the game.”
Iraola was relieved to get back on track after losing for the first time as Liverpool boss in the 3-0 defeat against Premier League leaders Manchester City on Sunday.
Iraola was also able to rest the likes of Vigil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister ahead of this weekend’s trip to Brentford.

“You have different demands for each game and you have to try to analyse what players, not just you can rest, it’s what players can perform well against LASK and help us to win the game, what players can help us against Brentford,” Iraola said.
“But after Brentford we will play in three days against Villarreal, another very difficult Champions League game, and we will need more than 11, more than 12, more than 13.” — AFP
5c22e7dcaab54b08: KUALA LUMPUR: Special allocations should be provided for boarding schools to fund full-time wardens as part of efforts to strengthen student safety and curb bullying, said Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.

He said a dedicated budget from the Education Ministry to appoint full-time wardens was important to ensure students could be monitored around the clock, particularly at night when most bullying cases in hostels were reported to occur.

Asyraf, who pioneered the appointment of former military personnel as full-time wardens at Mara Junior Science Colleges (MRSM), said relying on teachers to supervise students after school hours was no longer sufficient, given their existing workload and limited ability to monitor students until the early hours of the morning.

"In reality, how can teachers find the time to supervise these children 24 hours a day? They would have gone home by midnight at the latest, yet most bullying cases in hostels occur after that," he said.
As part of efforts to eradicate bullying at MRSM, a special online session on child-related laws was held for MRSM teachers on Tuesday night.

The online briefing, titled 'Safe MRSM: Students' Rights, Our Responsibility', was organised through a collaboration between Mara and the Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam), with 3,800 MRSM teachers nationwide taking part.
The session aimed to clarify the responsibilities of MRSM staff in ensuring a safe learning environment free from bullying and child exploitation.

Asyraf said the need for full-time wardens was not intended to question the Education Ministry's capabilities, but reflected the need for a more comprehensive solution to bullying to ensure residential schools remained a preferred option within the national education system.
He said the existing practice of appointing teachers as wardens, with a monthly allowance of RM300, should be reviewed as the additional responsibility added to their existing workload.
"Teachers not only have to teach during school hours, but their duties extend into the night as they supervise students in hostels.
"That is why teachers' rights and welfare must also be protected. We cannot expect teachers to carry out supervisory duties throughout the night without considering their workload," he said.
Introducing a different approach
Asyraf said Mara had introduced a different approach by appointing former military personnel as full-time wardens, who work daily from 7pm to 7am.
He said the initiative could serve as a reference for the Education Ministry in developing more effective monitoring mechanisms at residential schools under its purview.

Asyraf said Mara was prepared to share its experience and research findings on appointing former military personnel as wardens to assess whether the approach could be adopted at residential schools under the Education Ministry.

A pilot project involving the appointment of former military personnel as hostel wardens was previously reported to have been conducted by Universiti Putra Malaysia's (UPM) Institute for Social Science Studies (IPSAS) at Besut MRSM and Balik Pulau MRSM.
The 191-page study found positive responses from students, parents and administrators, alongside improvements in student discipline. No bullying cases were recorded throughout the pilot project.
The first phase involved 16 wardens who reported for duty at eight selected MRSM on July 1. Full implementation across all 58 MRSM is scheduled to begin on Jan 1, 2027.

Asyraf said the success of the approach was not a reason for Mara to be complacent, but should instead serve as a basis for evaluating the effectiveness of appointing full-time wardens in curbing bullying at residential schools.
"We are not being biased simply because Mara has appointed veterans or former military personnel as wardens. That is why we asked UPM to conduct a study on the matter.
"The screening process for wardens is also stringent, including checks to ensure candidates have no criminal records. Many former military personnel are still young and energetic," he said.
He said the presence of full-time wardens not only helped safeguard students but also contributed to better discipline and more structured daily routines.

ddfdc0812daafe5c: SAN FRANCISCO:The Federal Reserve will probably need to increase short-term interest rates further to rein in too-high inflation, San Francisco Federal Reserve president Mary Daly said on Wednesday, but she signaled there is no need to do so at the US central bank's Oct 27-28 meeting.

"We are more likely than not to need additional adjustments, but the timing of those adjustments to me is something we're still deliberating," Daly told Reuters in an exclusive interview. "I don't feel urgent that we have to decide with a limited set of information. I think we have the time that we need."

Several of Daly's colleagues have also signaled in recent weeks that the Fed is unlikely to raise rates this month. The Fed's policy rate is in the 3.75 per cent to four per cent range. Longer-term borrowing costs are even higher, with some — like 7.5 per cent mortgage rates — putting a damper on demand in some parts of the economy.

Daly said she feels financial markets understand the Fed's "reaction function," pointing to how traders responded to data earlier on Wednesday that showed consumer price inflation accelerated to 3.7 per cent in the 12 months through September, a bit faster than economists had anticipated. The Fed targets two per cent inflation by a different, but related, measure.

Though the initial reaction was "robust," she said — rate futures traders quickly piled into bets on an October Fed rate hike — investors "calmed" after parsing the data. Higher gasoline prices drove the overall increase, and underlying inflation, while still sticky, did not take a sharp turn upward.

"Definitely this data point suggests that the risk to inflation remains elevated," Daly said. "The risk to inflation has gone up more, but risks are not realities, and reacting on risk when you have time to make a good decision, to me, feels imprudent."
Daly said the labor market's continued stability gives the Fed room to focus on price stability.
But, she said, "Why force urgency when you don't need to have urgency? Why not take the time to be thoughtful and deliberate? And we have more meetings ahead of us."

Financial market pricing now puts about a 40 per cent chance of a second straight Fed rate hike at the central bank's next meeting, higher than before the data but no longer pointing to an increase as the most likely outcome, as was the case shortly after the inflation report was released.
The markets, she said, "understand that we're committed to price stability, and we will do what it takes to achieve it."

Policymakers "have a responsibility to communicate effectively to the public and be accountable, transparent and clear," she said. "The responsibility is to be crystal clear with people about what your objectives are, what you're accountable for and how you're going to balance the risks."

ec9e10fbcca6c9c2: SINGAPORE: Malaysian property tycoon Lee Yeow Seng is making waves as one of the most aggressive buyers of commercial real estate in Singapore, and he’s not done yet.

His IOI Properties Group Bhd is in exclusive talks and due diligence to purchase two property assets -- Chijmes, a retail venue inside a former Catholic convent in its civic district, and the nearby Capitol Kempinski hotel, chief executive officer Lee said in an interview. He declined to disclose how much a final agreement will value the two assets at, citing ongoing negotiations.

Singapore developer Perennial Holdings has been trying to sell the Kempinski hotel, which was being marketed for about S$600 million, according to people familiar with the matter. Chijmes was valued at S$379 million at the end of 2025.

IOI’s debt-fuelled buying spree has spurred a record year for real estate deals in Singapore. The firm is now courting investors for a new fund to ease the burden and give room for further expansion, as Lee seeks to challenge the wealthy clans that dominate the country’s property market.
“I’m a latecomer and I want to catch up with the rest,” the 47-year-old CEO said on the sidelines of a Forbes event in Singapore last week. “Most of them don’t share the vision of me.”

Perennial controls about a third of Chijmes, and about 80% of Capitol Singapore, a broader complex that contains the hotel, as well as a retail mall and residential units. A vehicle backed by an unnamed Southeast Asian sovereign wealth fund has a minority stake in both assets, corporate records show. Other Chijmes investors include local food chain Breadtalk Group Pte and Ronald Ooi, the former chair and CEO of Kim Eng, a stock brokerage.
Representatives for Perennial, which is backed by investors including palm oil tycoon Kuok Khoon Hong and Chinese private equity veteran Fang Fenglei, didn’t respond to requests for comment.

IOI is in talks to bring high-end fashion brands into Chijmes to raise rents, which have been depressed by a predominance of food and beverage outlets, said Lee. It also wants a global ultra-luxury hotel brand to replace the Kempinski, he said.

Lee’s Malaysia-listed firm, which has a large presence in its home country including one of the world’s largest malls, has splashed out on a range of Singapore properties in recent years. It gained full control of South Beach, an office complex that also houses his luxury penthouse and the JW Marriott hotel, after buying the majority stake from partner City Developments Ltd., which was looking to reduce debt. More recently, it bought office building Asia Square Tower 2, ballooning his commercial portfolio to S$10 billion.

It’s also looking to form a joint venture with CapitaLand Investment Ltd, a property manager backed by Temasek Holdings Pte, to buy One Raffles Place, people familiar with the matter said in August. The iconic office complex is majority-owned by OUE REIT, which confirmed last week that it’s in exclusive discussions with the firms on a potential sale.

IOI’s rapid acquisitions have fuelled a surge in its borrowings, with its net debt rising to 85% of equity as of end-June. In 2024, its board rebuffed a proposal by Lee to acquire Shenton House in Singapore, amid concerns about heavy capital commitments in Singapore and Malaysia. Lee, who is a scion of a wealthy palm oil family in Malaysia, made the purchase on his own.

The firm eventually agreed to acquire the office building and its liabilities this month to redevelop it. Even with a planned Malaysia real estate investment trust listing, that’s expected to raise the firm’s gearing further. Lee said he aims to reduce the net debt to 30%-50% of its equity in the next three to five years.
Private Fund

His plans largely hinge on the success of a private fund, which Lee said will be set up in two months. He’s tapped ex-Pimco Prime Real Estate executive Varun Singh to oversee the vehicle, which will initially include two assets totaling S$6 billion: the office portion of South Beach and the firm’s marquee office building IOI Central Boulevard Towers, whose tenants include Morgan Stanley and Jane Street Capital LLC.

Lee said the fund has courted investors including private equity firms, sovereign wealth funds and insurers, but declined to share names. It’s targeting an internal rate of return of 10%-11%, with semiannual distributions, he said.

The firm is looking to pare down its stake in the assets to about half, by marketing minimum holdings of about S$500 million with a five to seven-year lockup. It will look to inject more of its Singapore assets into the fund during that period, and eventually list it as a REIT.

Lee is more optimistic about real estate prospects in Singapore than rival financial hub Hong Kong, saying the former doesn’t have the baggage of being fully absorbed back into China in 2047 and will continue to be favored by the wealthy and global companies.

Still, other bets in Singapore have stumbled, including IOI’s plans to build a city center luxury residential project with 683 homes. The firm is liable to pay a higher tax, having sold only about 15 units there. Lee said he has secured a short-term reprieve from Singapore authorities to next April and will keep appealing against paying the charge.
The firm is pivoting toward renting out its units to expats, he said, blaming a 60% levy imposed on most foreigner purchases in 2023 for the poor sales.

But he remains undeterred in investing in Singapore, saying lenders and the company’s board remains supportive. “If I can expand, why should I hold myself back?” he said. “No one has asked me to slow down.”
c350bee0507b112e: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's federal deficit is projected to narrow from 3.6 per cent of GDP in 2026 to 3.3 per cent in 2027. Yet the deficit of the consolidated public sector is projected to widen from 6.0 to 7.0 per cent. Both figures deserve attention. They describe different parts of the same fiscal picture.

The distinction matters. An improvement in the Treasury's account does not, by itself, establish that the wider public sector is becoming more resilient. That judgement requires an examination of the institutions through which the state invests, delivers services and carries financial obligations.
One Treasury, a Wider Balance Sheet

The Ministry of Finance's Fiscal Outlook 2027 provides the framework. Its consolidated public-sector account combines general government with nonfinancial public corporations. General government includes the federal government, state governments, local governments and federal statutory bodies.
Transfers among the entities covered by the accounts are eliminated to avoid double counting.

The federal and consolidated deficits must therefore not be added together. The broader account already incorporates federal finances. It reveals the combined position after the necessary adjustments.
A dividend paid between two entities within these accounts illustrates the principle.

It changes where resources are held without creating additional income for the public sector as a whole. Similarly, a grant from one level of government to another is an internal transfer, rather than a fresh source of collective revenue.

The coverage still requires care. The description "government-linked" does not automatically place an institution within these accounts. Financial institutions and investment entities outside their coverage require separate scrutiny of their assets, obligations and potential calls on public support.

Consolidation also needs to be accompanied by attention to individual institutions. A combined surplus can coexist with financial stress in a particular entity. Resources held by one institution may be unavailable to meet another's obligations.
A Surplus Is Not a Free Pass

MOF projects the public sector's current surplus to decline from RM49.6 billion in 2026 to RM29.3 billion in 2027. Against development expenditure of RM191.4 billion, the latter leaves an overall deficit of RM162.1 billion. These published 2027 baseline estimates explicitly exclude new Budget 2027 measures, whose effects must be assessed separately.
A current surplus means that current receipts exceed operating expenditure. It does not establish that sufficient resources remain to finance the investment programme.
The gap still requires financing.

A wider deficit does not, however, prove that investment is excessive. Energy systems, transport networks and essential infrastructure may justify substantial expenditure. The test is whether projects are well chosen, delivered efficiently and financed on sustainable terms. Commercial investments need credible repayment capacity; projects serving public mandates need transparent arrangements for meeting their costs.

For debt sustainability, the primary balance—the overall balance excluding interest expenditure—must also be considered, together with existing debt, borrowing costs and economic growth. An operating surplus alone cannot establish whether debt is on a sustainable path.

The comparison must cover the same institutions: a public-sector balance cannot be assessed against federal debt alone. Nor does a financing requirement necessarily produce an identical increase in debt. The use of cash reserves, transactions in financial assets and changes in asset or liability values can affect the relationship.
Resilience Must Reach Every Institution

External uncertainty makes this broader assessment more consequential. Higher international yields can increase refinancing pressure, depending on domestic financing conditions, repayment schedules and currency exposure. Oil-price shocks may strengthen receipts in one institution while raising subsidy or operating costs elsewhere. Conflict, disrupted trade and severe climate events can weaken revenue while increasing expenditure needs.

The practical questions are straightforward. Which institutions must refinance soon? Which projects rely on continuing public support? Which guarantees could become direct government obligations if conditions deteriorate? Addressing these questions early creates room to respond before financial pressures constrain policy choices.

Malaysia would benefit from giving consolidated accounts greater prominence alongside the federal budget. Clear reporting of investment commitments, financing arrangements and contingent obligations would allow Parliament and the public to distinguish productive borrowing from mounting financial exposure.

Federal consolidation remains a worthwhile objective. Its achievement should be assessed alongside the strength of the institutions that undertake public investment and deliver essential services. Fiscal resilience must extend across those institutions, with each obligation understood and each risk assigned to an accountable decision-maker.
The Treasury's figures begin the assessment. The strength of the wider public sector completes it.

8ddd6c7f523dc627: KUALA LUMPUR: In business, success depends not only on how efficiently an organisation operates but also on whether it is pursuing the right objectives. This distinction is captured in a well-known management principle: effectiveness is doing the right things, while efficiency is doing things right. Although the two concepts are closely related, they represent different dimensions of organisational performance. A business may execute its activities with exceptional efficiency yet fail because it is pursuing the wrong objectives. Conversely, an organisation may identify the right opportunities but waste resources through poor execution.

Understanding this distinction is essential for boards of directors, senior management, operational leaders and internal auditors because it influences strategic decisions, resource allocation, risk management and long-term sustainability.
Doing the Right Things: The Importance of Effectiveness

Doing the right things means selecting objectives, priorities and activities that contribute meaningfully to the organisation's purpose and long-term success. It concerns what the organisation should do and whether its decisions will achieve the desired outcomes.

For example, a company may decide to enter a new market because of attractive growth prospects. Before committing substantial resources, its board and management must assess whether the market aligns with the company's strategy, whether sufficient capabilities exist, whether the expected returns justify the risks and whether the investment supports sustainable growth.
If the decision is fundamentally wrong, even excellent execution may not save the investment.

Similarly, a retailer may operate its stores efficiently, maintain tight cost controls and process transactions quickly. However, if consumer preferences shift towards online shopping and management fails to develop a suitable digital strategy, the business may gradually lose market share. Its operational efficiency cannot indefinitely compensate for a failure to recognise changing market conditions.
Doing the right things therefore requires sound judgement, strategic thinking, reliable information and the courage to challenge conventional assumptions.

For boards of directors, such a situation means asking whether management is pursuing the right strategy, investing in the right opportunities and managing the risks that could undermine the organisation's objectives.
Doing Things Right: The Importance of Efficiency
Doing things right means performing activities correctly, consistently and efficiently. It focuses on execution, productivity, quality, cost management and compliance with established procedures.

For example, a manufacturing company may improve production scheduling, reduce material wastage, automate repetitive tasks and introduce quality controls. These improvements enable the company to produce goods at a lower cost while maintaining acceptable quality standards.
Likewise, a finance department may streamline its reporting processes, reduce processing errors and shorten the time required to prepare financial statements.

Doing things right is important because poor execution wastes resources, increases operational risks and undermines customer confidence. Even a sound strategy can fail if employees lack the necessary skills, processes are unreliable or management cannot implement decisions effectively.
Internal controls, standard operating procedures, performance indicators and staff training all contribute to doing things right.

Nevertheless, efficiency must be evaluated in the context of the intended outcome. Producing more goods is not necessarily an achievement if demand is declining, just as reducing expenditure is not beneficial if it compromises product quality, cybersecurity or regulatory compliance.
When Efficiency Becomes a Problem
One of the greatest dangers in business is becoming so focused on efficiency that management loses sight of effectiveness.

Consider a bank that reduces operating costs by closing branches and directing customers towards digital services. The strategy may improve efficiency. However, if the bank fails to consider customer needs, digital accessibility, cybersecurity and service quality, the cost savings may be offset by customer dissatisfaction, fraud losses and reputational damage.

Another example is a company that achieves its annual profit target by postponing equipment maintenance, reducing employee training or cutting essential quality inspections. In the short term, expenses decline and reported profitability may improve. In the longer term, equipment failures, workplace accidents, product defects and operational disruptions may increase.

These examples illustrate a crucial lesson: doing things right does not necessarily mean doing the right things. Efficiency can make a flawed decision more damaging by enabling the organisation to pursue the wrong course of action faster and at a greater scale.
Implications for Boards and Management

Boards should ensure that management does not confuse operational performance with strategic success. Achieving budgets, meeting production targets and reducing costs are important, but these measures alone do not establish whether the organisation is moving in the right direction.
Directors should ask questions such as:
*Are our strategic priorities aligned with changing market conditions?
*Are we investing sufficient resources in future growth and emerging risks?
*Are our performance indicators measuring meaningful outcomes or merely activities?
*Are short-term savings creating long-term risks?
*Should we stop, modify or reconsider activities that no longer create value?
Management, in turn, must translate strategic objectives into practical plans, establish appropriate controls, allocate resources effectively and monitor results.

Internal auditors can contribute by examining both dimensions. They should assess not only whether processes operate efficiently and controls function as intended, but also whether activities support organisational objectives and whether the risks associated with those objectives are appropriately managed.

This does not mean internal audits should make strategic decisions on management's behalf. Rather, it should provide independent assurance and insights that help the board and management evaluate whether resources are being used appropriately and objectives are being pursued effectively.
Achieving the Right Balance

The most successful organisations combine effectiveness with efficiency. They first establish what needs to be achieved and why, then determine how to achieve it with the best use of available resources.

Effectiveness should generally guide strategic direction, while efficiency should improve execution. Both require regular review because business conditions, customer expectations, technology and regulatory requirements change over time.

Organisations should also recognise that doing the right things sometimes requires difficult decisions: abandoning an unprofitable business, investing in preventive controls, improving employee capabilities or accepting short-term costs to protect long-term value.
Such decisions may reduce immediate efficiency but improve overall effectiveness and resilience.
Conclusion
The distinction between doing the right things and doing things right is more than a management slogan. It is a fundamental principle of sound business decision-making.
Doing the right things ensures that an organisation pursues appropriate objectives, while doing things right ensures that those objectives are achieved efficiently and competently.

Ultimately, effectiveness determines whether an organisation is heading in the right direction; efficiency determines how well it travels that path. A business needs both. Without effectiveness, efficiency may simply accelerate failure. Without efficiency, even the right strategy may be undermined by waste and poor execution.

The real test of good management is not merely whether the organisation performs its activities well, but whether those activities create sustainable value for shareholders, customers, employees and other stakeholders.

b42e1c8397d0604d: PETALING JAYA: Breast cancer can feel frightening because no woman can completely control whether it happens. Ageing, family history, genes and reproductive history all play a part.
The World Health Organisation states that most breast cancers occur in women with no modifiable risk factor apart from being female and over 40.
This clearly shows that a breast cancer diagnosis is never a woman’s fault. Yet “not completely preventable” does not mean “nothing you do matters”.
Your daily habits can help lower risk and support overall health.
For women who have completed breast cancer treatment, similar habits may support recovery and long-term wellbeing, to complement your regular follow-up care with your specialist.
Think overall food pattern, not just ‘anti-cancer’ superfood
No juice, herb or supplement can prevent breast cancer. What matters more is the pattern of foods you eat repeatedly.
Build your meals around vegetables, fruit, beans, lentils and wholegrains, with sensible portions of lean protein.

This can still look wonderfully Malaysian, such as brown or mixed-grain rice with ikan bakar and ulam; chapati with dhal and vegetables; yong tau foo noodle soup with extra greens; or oats with fruit and nuts.
These foods provide fibre and antioxidant plant compounds that support health. They also make meals satisfying.
You do not need to ban rice, noodles or favourite family dishes. Adjust the balance of your meals by including more vegetables, enough protein and some carbohydrates.
After menopause, weight deserves gentle attention
The connection between body weight and breast cancer is not about appearance.

After menopause, fat tissue becomes an important source of oestrogen. Higher levels of body fat may also affect insulin and inflammation, which are signals that can encourage some cancer cells to grow.

The aim is not crash dieting. If weight loss is your goal, gradual changes are more realistic, such as reducing sugary drinks, serving slightly smaller portions, cooking at home more often and limiting mindless snacking.
For breast cancer survivors, weight changes can be affected by treatment and menopause. Seek personalised advice from a dietitian rather than struggling alone.
Move in ways that fit real life
Regular physical activity is linked with a lower risk of breast cancer, both before and after menopause. It can help regulate hormones, insulin, inflammation and body fat.
Work towards 150 minutes of moderate activity each week, and add muscle-strengthening exercise twice weekly. Brisk walking, dancing, gardening, housework and taking the stairs all count.
Start where you are. A 10-minute walk after lunch and another after dinner is meaningful. Consistency matters more than an impressive workout you cannot maintain.
Be honest about alcohol
Alcohol is a proven breast cancer risk factor; even small amounts can increase risk. The body converts alcohol into a substance that can damage cells, and alcohol can also raise oestrogen levels.

For cancer prevention, not drinking alcohol offers the lowest risk. If alcohol is part of your social life, reduce how often and how much you drink. Choose an alcohol-free option at gatherings without feeling that you owe anyone an explanation.
What about survivors?

If you have had breast cancer, do not begin strict diets, high-dose supplements or traditional remedies without discussing them with your oncology team. “Natural” does not always mean safe, and some products can interfere with treatment.

Evidence for preventing recurrence through one specific food remains limited. Current guidance encourages survivors, when medically able, to follow the same broad cancer-prevention pattern which is eating nourishing meals, getting regular physical activity, maintaining a healthy weight and consuming very little or no alcohol. Your plan should be adapted to your treatment, symptoms and recovery.
Finally, healthy living does not replace screening or medical care. Attend recommended breast screening, know what is normal for your breasts and have any new lump or change checked promptly.

Breast cancer prevention is not about living fearfully or eating perfectly. It is about giving yourself more protection through small choices that are repeated and treating your body with care, not blame.

Indra Balaratnam is a consultant dietitian and a fellow of the Malaysian Dietitians’ Association. She runs her own private practice, Indra Balaratnam Nutrition, in Kuala Lumpur. Connect with her on Facebook and Instagram.
1785e68a2dda3857: PETALING JAYA: Umno appears to be seeking a shortcut to gaining ground in the four PAS-dominated states, collectively known as SG4, by challenging the Islamic party to give up a third of the seats there to demonstrate its sincerity, an analyst says.

Syaza Shukri of the International Islamic University Malaysia said the demand by Umno Supreme Council member Nur Jazlan Mohamed was clearly a manoeuvre to help the Barisan Nasional linchpin regain some ground in Kedah, Terengganu, Kelantan and Perlis.
“I see this really as Umno looking for an easy way to break through, especially in states like Terengganu and Kedah, where its influence has long been on the decline," she told FMT.
Syaza said the demand appeared unfair when Umno did not make room for PAS in the Johor and Negeri Sembilan polls and was unlikely to do so in the Nov 14 Melaka state election.
“I don’t think it is fair to put PAS through this test of sincerity. Has Umno shown its sincerity? It feels one-sided to put it on PAS just because it holds a dominant position there,” she said.

“I know there’s a lot of talk about PAS’s history of abandoning its partners, but Umno has a history of being overly dominant as well. So, if Umno wants to make demands on PAS, it’s only fair for Umno to be ‘tested’ too.”
Umno led the Perlis government until 2022 when PAS wrested control of the state. PAS has also established Kelantan as its stronghold although Umno led the state from 1978 to 1990.
Meanwhile, the Kedah and Terengganu state governments have changed hands between Umno and PAS several times.
The Islamic party has nonetheless tightened its grip on all four states, with its Perikatan Nasional coalition sweeping most, if not all, parliamentary and state seats there in 2022 and 2023.
By comparison, Umno currently has only two elected representatives across all four states, specifically two assemblymen in Kelantan.
On Sunday, Nur Jazlan said PAS should allocate one-third of the seats in the four states to Umno to demonstrate its sincerity in pursuing Malay unity.
Akademi Nusantara’s Azmi Hassan said Nur Jazlan’s statement would throw a spanner in the works in the negotiations between Umno and PAS, especially in Kedah where Umno is seeking to make a comeback.

Azmi said it was clear that Kedah Umno leaders were upset with Nur Jazlan’s statement, especially since the northern state was difficult territory for the party and PAS has established dominance there.
“His statement makes it difficult for Kedah Umno to negotiate the terms of its cooperation with PAS,” he added.
8987fa60a1084fa6: PETALING JAYA: Umno dilihat cuba mencari jalan pintas untuk menembusi kubu empat negeri diperintah PAS dikenali SG4 dengan mencabar parti Islam itu memperuntukkan satu pertiga kerusi kepadanya sebagai bukti keikhlasan dalam penyatuan Melayu, kata penganalisis.

Syaza Shukri daripada Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia (UIAM) berkata, tuntutan Ahli Majlis Kerja Tertinggi Umno, Nur Jazlan Mohamed, jelas langkah untuk membantu Barisan Nasional (BN) meraih semula pengaruh di Kedah, Terengganu, Kelantan dan Perlis.
“Saya melihat ini sebagai usaha Umno mencari jalan mudah untuk menembusi negeri seperti Terengganu dan Kedah, tempat di mana pengaruhnya sudah lama merosot,” katanya kepada FMT.
Syaza berkata, tuntutan itu tidak adil kerana Umno tidak memberi laluan kepada PAS dalam PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan, selain dijangka tidak berbuat demikian pada PRN Melaka 14 Nov ini.

Umno menguasai Perlis sehingga 2022 sebelum PAS mengambil alih negeri itu. PAS turut mengukuhkan Kelantan sebagai kubunya selepas memerintah negeri itu sejak 1990, menggantikan Umno yang mentadbir dari 1978.
Di Kedah dan Terengganu pula, kerajaan negeri beberapa kali bertukar tangan antara Umno dan PAS.

Namun, PAS semakin mengukuhkan cengkamannya di keempat-empat negeri itu apabila Perikatan Nasional (PN) menyapu sebahagian besar, jika tidak hampir semua, kerusi Parlimen dan DUN dalam pilihan raya pada 2022 dan 2023.

Pada Ahad, Nur Jazlan berkata PAS perlu memperuntukkan satu pertiga kerusi di empat negeri berkenaan kepada Umno sebagai bukti keikhlasan dalam usaha menyatukan orang Melayu.
Sementara itu, Azmi Hassan daripada Akademi Nusantara berkata kenyataan Nur Jazlan boleh menjejaskan rundingan kerjasama Umno-PAS, terutama di Kedah yang mahu ditawan semula parti tersebut.
Katanya, pemimpin Umno Kedah jelas tidak senang dengan kenyataan itu kerana negeri berkenaan adalah medan sukar bagi parti tersebut, manakala PAS sudah mengukuhkan penguasaannya.
“Kenyataan itu menyukarkan Umno Kedah merundingkan syarat kerjasama dengan PAS,” katanya.

de1c79ed13fff882: MANCHESTER: Manchester City's 4-2 defeat by Paris St Germain told only part of the story of Enzo Maresca's first loss as City boss, with his men staggering through the first half before roaring back after the break.

Playing their first home game since an independent commission found them guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules, City were staring at a rout when a rampant PSG raced into a 3-0 lead with a first-half masterclass.
Maresca's side tore into the visitors after halftime, pouring forward with an intensity and urgency that had been entirely absent in the opening 45 minutes.
Erling Haaland spearheaded the fightback, scoring twice to become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the mark in just 60 games, 20 quicker than Lionel Messi.

City kept coming. They finished with nearly twice as many shots as PSG and around three times as many touches in the opposition box, while recording a higher expected-goals figure at both halftime and fulltime. PSG, though, were more ruthless.

"I think we start quite good until the first goal (from Desire Doue in the 13th minute) and then we concede the second one (Ousmane Dembele) after one minute. That created some bad feelings," Maresca told TNT Sports.
"Second half, we were much better and probably deserved something more."

City had arrived on the back of a 3-0 thrashing of Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday and Maresca felt they generated enough chances to salvage something even after digging themselves a three-goal hole.

"Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more," he said. "Luis (Enrique, PSG's manager) said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky today.
"You have to be clinical but not lose the balance," Maresca said.

The defeat unfolded against a backdrop of turmoil stretching far beyond City, with the fallout from the seismic verdict over the 114 breaches sending shockwaves through the Premier League and making City the villains of English football in the eyes of many.
They have denied wrongdoing and have appealed.
On the pitch, they remain three points clear of Arsenal atop the Premier League table ahead of Saturday's home game against Ipswich.
Asked if he had a message for supporters, Maresca said: "We are sorry for the first half for sure. Saturday is a Premier League game and we need to continue our run."
696867bff1dfec86: BATU PAHAT: A Form Four student will be charged in the magistrate's court today with murdering 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal at a hall in a secondary school in Yong Peng on Oct 3.

b3315e7c2b9a143c: WASHINGTON: The FBI denied a US media report Wednesday that its director was visiting Russia, insisting that Kash Patel was at an event at a university in Virginia.
US news broadcaster MS Now reported that Patel had landed in Russia for a scheduled meeting just weeks before crucial US midterm elections, citing two people familiar with the matter.
But the FBI said in a post on X that the report was wrong: "Here's where Kash Patel actually is...Liberty U, doing a law enforcement appreciation event."
Video posted on YouTube on Wednesday from an ABC affiliate showed Patel speaking on a panel at the Liberty University School of Law in Lynchburg, Virginia.

The back-and-forth comes days after US President Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin wanted to reach a deal on the war with Ukraine, accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky of resisting a compromise.
Trump has repeatedly lashed out at Zelensky, a major pro-Western leader in Europe, even saying he should be replaced as president.
Trump has also often declined to criticise Putin, often putting himself out of step with members of his own Republican Party even as Putin ramps up attacks against Ukraine.
Last week, Trump angered Ukraine's European allies with news of a deal to buy heavily sanctioned Russia diesel in order to lower domestic US prices -- a key issue ahead of the Nov 3 midterms.
On Tuesday, a dozen Republican and Democratic senators urged Trump to scrap that deal, calling it a betrayal of Ukraine that would bankroll Moscow's war effort.

Speculation that Patel might travel to Moscow has swirled ever since Politico reported in July that the FBI director planned a trip to Russia, likely in mid-October, citing people familiar with the matter.
Last week, The Atlantic reported there was a quiet campaign at the FBI, as well as opposition from two senior House Democrats, to cancel the trip.
In August, CIA Director John Ratcliffe made a highly unusual visit to Moscow, apparently to warn Russia against any attack on Nato, US media reported.
82b164220bcc5ed0: SAN ISIDRO: Diego Maradona's family on Wednesday called for his medical team to be given stiff prison terms over what two of his daughters called his "murder."
Seven medical professionals have been on trial since April over Maradona's death on November 25, 2020, while convalescing after surgery for a brain clot.
The star of the 1986 World Cup died aged 60 of heart failure and acute pulmonary edema, two weeks after going under the knife.
His medical team is accused of providing grossly inadequate care in the lead-up to his death at a private home rented for his convalescence.
Maradona's family are divided on the severity of the punishment they believe his carers should face.
A lawyer for two of his daughters, Dalma and Gianinna, on Wednesday accused his carers of "murder" and asked that six of the seven accused be sentenced to up to 15 years in prison.
"They killed a mythological hero," lawyer Fernando Burlando said, accusing the defendants of "brutal indifference" to the icon's fate.
Counsel for the champion's three sisters Rita, Claudia and Ana, sought terms of up to 10 years for five of the seven defendants.
Their lawyer Pablo Jurado called for medical coordinator Nancy Forlini to receive the harshest punishment.
On Tuesday, a lawyer for Maradona's youngest son, 13-year-old Diego Fernando Maradona, had called for the player's personal physician Leopoldo Luque and Forlini to be each given 16-year sentences.
State prosecutors kicked off the closing arguments last week with a call for guilty findings against six of the seven accused and prison sentences ranging from four to 12 years.
They added that Luque should receive the stiffest punishment.
The closing arguments are set to continue until the end of October.
The court in the Buenos Aires suburb of San Isidro, near where Maradona died, is then expected to reserve its judgement to a later date.
6fcf64c22ca58021: Dalam tulisan terdahulu, saya berhujah Akta Hasutan 1948 wajar diisytiharkan tidak sah oleh mahkamah, melainkan Parlimen meminda Perlembagaan Persekutuan bagi membenarkan secara jelas sekatan terhadap kebebasan bersuara seperti diperuntukkan dalam akta itu.
Ogos lalu, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim sendiri menggesa undang-undang warisan penjajah itu dimansuhkan supaya kemerdekaan negara benar-benar bermakna.

Lebih menarik, gesaan itu dibuat pada acara sambutan kemerdekaan di Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM). Ini bukan perkara kecil, memandangkan Pakatan Harapan (PH) yang dipimpinnya juga sudah sekian lama memperjuangkan pemansuhan akta tersebut.
Namun, sehingga kini, tiada tindakan diambil pemimpin politik untuk menunaikan janji itu.
Akibatnya, undang-undang yang menyekat kebebasan bersuara secara keterlaluan itu terus berkuat kuasa, walaupun sudah lama sepatutnya dimansuhkan, dan masih boleh digunakan terhadap rakyat biasa.
Mungkin ahli politik ketika ini mempunyai keutamaan lain atau tidak melihat sebarang kepentingan untuk membawa rang undang-undang bagi memansuhkan akta tersebut.
Walaupun Dewan Rakyat sedang bersidang, tumpuan ketika ini lebih terarah kepada Rang Undang-undang Perbekalan bagi membiayai perbelanjaan kerajaan pada 2027.
Jadi, apakah pilihan yang masih ada kepada rakyat?
Peguam negara yang bertanggungjawab menjaga kepentingan awam boleh mengemukakan permohonan kepada Mahkamah Persekutuan supaya Akta Hasutan diisytiharkan tidak sah.
Namun, sikap berdiam diri beliau setakat ini memberi gambaran perkara itu bukan dalam senarai keutamaannya.
Adakah Majlis Peguam, badan bukan kerajaan (NGO), aktivis atau orang awam akan mengambil inisiatif mencabar kesahihan akta itu? Tiada siapa yang tahu.

Bagaimanapun, seperti yang sering saya tegaskan, mahkamah mempunyai kuasa yang mencukupi di bawah Perlembagaan untuk menangani kebuntuan ini apabila wakil rakyat yang dipilih gagal mengambil tindakan.

Pada pandangan saya, prinsip undang-undang berkaitan sumpah jawatan hakim dan kuasa kehakiman, apabila ditafsir bersama Perkara 4 Perlembagaan Persekutuan, sudah menyediakan asas yang kukuh untuk pengamal undang-undang membawa cabaran terhadap kesahihan Akta Hasutan ke mahkamah.
Ini termasuk meminta mahkamah menggunakan kuasanya untuk mengambil tindakan atas inisiatif sendiri, yang dikenali sebagai 'suo motu'.
Sumpah jawatan yang mewajibkan hakim memelihara, melindungi dan mempertahankan hak rakyat di bawah Perlembagaan bukan sekadar menuntut mereka menghalang pencabulan hak tersebut.
Sebaliknya, sumpah itu turut meletakkan tanggungjawab kepada hakim untuk memastikan rakyat benar-benar dapat menggunakan dan menikmati hak yang dijamin Perlembagaan.
Pada hemat saya, usaha membawa perkara ini ke mahkamah tidak sepatutnya terhalang oleh prosedur yang terlalu rumit.
Mengambil contoh amalan di India, sepucuk surat kepada Mahkamah Tinggi atau Mahkamah Persekutuan sepatutnya sudah memadai untuk memulakan proses kehakiman.

Ini kerana, menurut tafsiran saya, kuasa mahkamah untuk bertindak dalam keadaan sedemikian berpunca secara langsung daripada sumpah jawatan hakim, bukannya daripada Perkara 121(1) Perlembagaan Persekutuan.
Bagaimanapun, mahkamah tidak sepatutnya membuat keputusan tanpa mendapatkan pandangan pihak berkepentingan.

Mahkamah wajar mengundang peguam negara, Badan Peguam Malaysia, Persatuan Peguam Bela Sarawak dan Persatuan Undang-undang Sabah untuk memberikan pandangan sama ada Akta Hasutan boleh terus berkuat kuasa dalam sistem perundangan yang menjunjung Keluhuran Perlembagaan.

Tiada siapa boleh menuduh mahkamah bertindak sesuka hati atau melampaui kuasanya, lebih-lebih lagi apabila pemimpin politik sendiri sudah menyatakan secara terbuka hasrat untuk memansuhkan akta berkenaan.
Persoalannya, adakah pengamal undang-undang bersedia mengambil langkah untuk mencabar akta itu?
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
224644dc9cbab55b: KUALA LUMPUR: Nigeria may be thousands of kilometres from Malaysia, but one woman’s love for West African fashion has led not only to a business of her own but to the Nigerian man she would eventually marry.

Shantarubini Kalaithasan, better known as Rubini, was already wearing Ankara prints before she met her husband, Zibai Williams Achi. Today, the Malaysian Indian and Nigerian couple run Ankara by Sutra Trading, a Kuala Lumpur-based business specialising in West African clothing.

Rubini, a former banker turned financial coach, first discovered African fashion out of personal interest. “I attend an African-led church in Ampang, where I would see people wearing these unique and vibrant prints. That was actually the first time I came across them,” she told FMT Lifestyle.

Among the textiles that caught her eye were Ankara, a factory-printed cotton fabric known for its bold wax-resist patterns, and Adire, a traditionally hand-dyed textile originating from Nigeria’s Yoruba people.

With help from Nigerian friends, Rubini initially ordered clothes for herself. When colleagues began asking where she had bought the eye-catching pieces, she realised there might be a business opportunity.
She began selling small quantities online around 2020 before taking the clothes to bazaars. The garments are made and tailored in Nigeria, supporting local artisans there.
According to Zibai, most of these sellers are not businessmen or women; "they are artisans just trying to make ends meet in a difficult economy".
Rubini’s fondness for African fashion caught Zibai’s attention after his elder sister, who had been living in Malaysia for years, showed him her social media profile.
“I saw a photo of her and I asked my sister, ‘Who is that? She looks good in Ankara!’ My sister said, ‘What’s beautiful, the Ankara or the girl?’ I said, ‘Both'," he told FMT Lifestyle with a laugh.
After getting to know each other through text messages, the pair met in person in late 2022 and married in October 2024.

Their wedding celebrated both cultures, with Rubini wearing a lehenga for the Indian ceremony before changing into Nigerian attire, while Zibai wore an Indian jippa before switching to a traditional West African agbada.

That blending of cultures has also found its way into their business. Ankara and Adire remain at its heart, with ready-made kimonos, skirts, dresses and men’s T-shirts sold alongside custom-made pieces.
Additionally, Rubini is currently exploring designs that combine both Nigerian and Indian influences.
She also tries to keep prices relatively affordable, noting that Ankara garments in Malaysia can easily cost upward of RM200.

Their customers include Malaysians and Singaporeans, as well as Algerians, Egyptians and Nigerians living here. “We also have government officials here who like to pair our pieces with local batik,” Rubini said, noting that their pieces can be dressed up or worn more casually.
In 2024, the couple expanded beyond fashion, adding products such as raw shea butter, African black soap and raw honey.

Their latest venture is African Pantry, which made its debut at Malaysia VegFest 9.0 last month. The couple served vegan versions of egusi with fufu, jollof rice, puff puff and zobo - and quickly discovered there was plenty of appetite for them.
“On the second day of VegFest, Rubini had to come back home to cook because we ran out of food by 1pm. I was thinking, ‘Who is eating all this food?’” Zibai said.
Customers began asking where they could find the food after the festival, prompting the couple to consider turning African Pantry into a more permanent venture, possibly even a café.
“I like Malaysian food as well, so it felt good to see people here showing an interest in and appreciating my culture and food,” Zibai added.
Although Zibai’s two years in Malaysia have not been without challenges, he said the welcome he received from Rubini’s family was an unexpected source of comfort.
“They were very supportive from the beginning, and I was so surprised with how close-knit they were,” he shared.
That support was easy to see at VegFest, where Rubini’s mother and aunt helped out at the African Pantry booth.

For now, the couple continue to operate mainly online from Sentul, but they hope to eventually grow Ankara by Sutra Trading into a physical boutique, while seeing just how far their food venture might take them.
Follow Ankara by Sutra Trading on Instagram.
02a66f5cbb6850a8: In a previous column, I had argued that the Sedition Act 1948 ought to be struck down unless Parliament amends the Federal Constitution to expressly incorporate it as a permitted restriction on free speech.
As recently as in August, the prime minister himself called for this colonial-era law to be repealed to truly give meaning to Malaysia’s independence.
The fact that the remarks were made at a Merdeka event in UiTM was not lost on me. After all, his Pakatan Harapan coalition has also long championed the cause.
Despite that, to date, no action has been taken by our political leaders to fulfil this pledge.
That has kept the draconian law, which significantly curtails freedom of speech, on the statute books well past its expiry date, and still available for use against ordinary citizens.

Perhaps, our politicians have other priorities presently— or maybe they have no incentive to push the necessary bill to repeal the law. The Dewan Rakyat may be in session, but its present focus is the supply bill to fund the government for 2027.

So what recourse does the rakyat have? The attorney-general (AG), being the guardian of public interest, could move a motion in the Federal Court asking for the Act to be struck down. However, his silence thus far suggests that that item is nowhere on his agenda.
Will the Bar Council, an NGO, activists or a member of the public pick the matter up? No one knows.
Yet, as I have consistently maintained, the courts possess ample constitutional authority to move the dial given the inertia shown by our elected representatives.

In my view the jurisprudence related to oath of office and constitutional judicial power read with Article 4 is ripe enough for the legal community to bring forth strategic constitutional challenges before the relevant courts, including by inviting the court to exercise its suo motu powers.

The oath of office, which binds judges to “preserve, protect and defend” the constitutional rights of all Malaysians, imposes upon the courts a sacred duty not merely to safeguard those rights, but to actively facilitate their empowerment.

In my view, the process should involve very little red tape. Following the practice in India, a letter to the High Court or the Federal Court should be sufficient to set the wheels of justice in motion—since the judicial power invoked is exercised directly according to the oath of office and not under Article 121(1).

However, the courts should not act on its own. It should invite the AG, the Malaysian Bar, the Advocates Association of Sarawak, and the Sabah Law Society to weigh in on whether the Sedition Act can truly coexist within the constitutional supremacy regime.
No one can accuse the courts of going rogue, especially since our political leaders have already expressed publicly an intention to do the very same thing.
So, will the legal industry make an attempt?
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

4922a7f0dc2ea621: ROME: Jose Mourinho hit out at the "shameless" decision by Spanish football authorities to announce that Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior had been slapped with a four-match ban just hours before their Champions League clash with Roma kicked off.
The Brazil international was handed the punishment on Wednesday after being sent off during Saturday's 1-0 LaLiga win over Villarreal for pulling the hair of an opponent.

It is a costly ban, depriving Mourinho of one of his star attackers for an important run of league games that includes a Clasico clash with rivals Barcelona, who hold a six-point lead over Real at the summit of the table.
Vinicius started as Mourinho's side pulled off an incredible late comeback to beat Roma 4-3 in the Champions League, having trailed 3-1 with seven minutes remaining.
But the Portuguese made his feelings clear about how the timing of the announcement had disrupted preparations in a post-match press conference.

Mourinho said: "Do you think it's normal that a player from a Spanish team, who has to play a match that is also important for Spanish football, that two hours before the match a player knows he's been given a four-match suspension?
"Couldn't they do it now? Couldn't they do it tomorrow morning? Do we have to come by bus and almost arrive at the stadium when we find out Vinicius has a four-match suspension?"
Mourinho added: "They do things shamelessly now. The cat is out of the bag now. Two hours before the match, a player must know he has a four-match suspension.

"A Spanish team that has earned three points for Spanish football, for the rankings, for the prestige of Spanish football. You want to kill a player two hours before the match; it doesn't seem normal to me."
Scheduling complaints
Mourinho also highlighted his unhappiness with scheduling, with his side set to face AEK Athens in the Greek capital on Nov 4, before travelling to Valencia in La Liga on Nov 7.
Asked what the Vinicius ban announcement says, Mourinho replied: "At the very least, a lack of respect.
"Playing in Athens on Wednesday night, arriving in Madrid probably at 5am, something like that, and then playing Saturday in Valencia, on a weekend that precedes a week of national team matches.
"It makes absolutely no sense, they make you play on Saturday in Valencia, which is an extremely difficult match, it doesn't seem innocent to me.

"The usual excuses, I don't buy them, because this wasn't 25 years ago. The excuses from TV, that it was TV that decided, that it was TV that chose the match for Saturday, I don't buy this anymore. I'm too old to swallow this.

"And this Vinicius story, two hours before a match, knowing that he has a four-match suspension, doesn't deserve comment. Real Madrid fans aren't stupid and I will do everything possible to open people's eyes."
It was a good night for Mourinho on the pitch, as his substitutions turned the game in Real's favour after they were outplayed for much of the game until the closing stages.

Donyell Malen's double had given Roma a 3-1 lead early in the second half, but two of Mourinho's substitutes scored, Endrick and Carlos Espi, and another, Arda Guler, provided two assists in the late rally.
"I'm not going to be a genius and say I had prepared everything for a 3-1 to 4-3 victory, it's not true," Mourinho said.
"But I genuinely thought that in the last 20 minutes I had substitutions I could make, and I had substitutions that could change things."
b0ee67d907692dac: JERUSALEM: The former head of Israel's Shin Bet domestic security agency sued Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for defamation on Wednesday, weeks before elections, in a row over responsibility for Hamas's Oct 7, 2023, attack.

Netanyahu, who polls show is in a tight race to stay in power in the Oct 27 election, has faced heavy criticism from the opposition for failing to prevent the attack, the deadliest day in Israeli history.

Netanyahu, who has cast himself as a guarantor of Israel's security over his decades-long career, has insisted that he could have stopped the attack had the Shin Bet's then director, Ronen Bar, or military leaders called to wake him up on the day of the early-morning assault.
In the 134-page court document, Bar accused Netanyahu of "lying to cover himself" and said it was slanderous to accuse him of "criminal failures" over the attack.
Netanyahu made accusations against Bar "that he knew to be false, with the aim of diverting the debate from his own responsibility for the events of Oct 7", the lawsuit said.
Instead, it was Netanyahu's policies over several years that had "increased the dangers posed by terrorist organisations in Gaza", it said.
Bar resigned in June 2025, saying at the time that "all the systems collapsed" in the security agency and that Shin Bet "failed to sound the alarm".
But Bar said he was resigning to take responsibility as head of the organisation and insists he did warn Netanyahu before Oct 7 of potential threats linked to Hamas.
Bar is seeking three million shekels (around US$968,500) in damages from Netanyahu.
Bar said he telephoned the prime minister's military secretary as soon as signs of a possible attack emerged, but that he did not have Netanyahu's direct number.
"Ronen, are you serious?" Netanyahu responded in a statement issued by his Likud party on Wednesday.
"You had my number on the red line and could have called me immediately, as all security chiefs do."
"How many lives could we have saved if only you had called in time?" he asked.

Hamas stormed into Israel with pickup trucks and paragliders and opened fire at sites including a music festival. The attack killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures, while fighters also dragged 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of whom were already dead.

Israel responded with a massive offensive in Gaza that has killed more than 74,300 people, according to the territory's health ministry, which operates under Hamas and whose figures are generally considered reliable by the United Nations.
dc5956d7e5730055: KUALA LUMPUR: Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun made an uninspiring return to the World Tour as a reunited partnership after crashing out in the Denmark Open first round in Odense on Wednesday.
The world No. 12, who were ranked as high as No. 4 last year, suffered a disappointing 21-16, 22-20 defeat to Denmark's world No. 28 Christian Faust Kjaer-Rasmus Kjaer in 38 minutes.
It was a frustrating outcome for Wei Chong-Kai Wun, who had comfortably beaten the same opponents 21-11, 21-16 at last year's Australian Open.
Their early exit stood in contrast to Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik, another established partnership restored following national men's doubles coach Herry Iman Pierngadi's experimental reshuffle.
Aaron-Wooi Yik marked their official reunion on Tuesday with an impressive three-game victory over defending champions and former world champions Takuro Hoki-Yugo Kobayashi of Japan.
Both Malaysian combinations had been temporarily separated earlier this year as Herry experimented with alternative partnerships in search of stronger options for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Interestingly, Wei Chong and Kai Wun both enjoyed encouraging spells with their respective temporary partners.
Kai Wun formed a particularly successful combination with Yap Roy King, winning the Korea Masters in August before reaching the China Masters semi-finals the following month.
Wei Chong, meanwhile, partnered Wooi Yik and reached the Korea Masters final, where they were beaten by none other than Kai Wun-Roy King.

Wei Chong-Kai Wun briefly reunited for the World Championships in New Delhi in August, reaching the last 16, but their latest setback raises questions over how quickly they can rediscover their chemistry.
Before the reshuffle, they had shown considerable consistency, reaching the quarter-finals of the Malaysia Open, India Open, Indonesia Masters and All England earlier this season.
They will now need a much-improved showing at next week's French Open, another Super 750 event, to demonstrate that their renewed partnership can still challenge the world's leading combinations.
Meanwhile, world No. 6 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin made light work of compatriots Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub-Tan Wee Kiong, winning 21-14, 21-11 in just 27 minutes.
The sixth seeds are looking to regain momentum after a relatively subdued run since lifting the Indonesia Open title in June.
They have not reached another final since, with their more recent campaigns, including a first-round exit at the China Masters and a quarter-final finish at the Asian Games.
There was also good news for Chia Weijie-Teo Ee Yi, who defeated Taiwan's world No. 32 Chen Zhi Ray-Lin Yu Chieh 21-16, 21-15 in 30 minutes.

The world No. 58, who formed their partnership earlier this year, will face Sze Fei-Izzuddin in an all-Malaysian second-round clash today, guaranteeing Malaysia at least one men's doubles quarter-final berth.
In women's singles, world No. 37 Wong Ling Ching put up a brave fight before falling 19-21, 21-11, 21-19 to Japan's world No. 21 Riko Gunji in 67 minutes.
It was her third defeat in as many meetings against Gunji, extending the Japanese player's unbeaten head-to-head record against the Malaysian.

911cfb84e1ac024d: WASHINGTON: The White House was facing mounting questions on Wednesday over new press secretary Katie Zacharia's legal credentials, after a faltering first day in the job when she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam.

A US watchdog group filed a complaint with the State Bar of California, asking it to investigate whether President Donald Trump's spokeswoman — the public face of the administration — had broken the law by repeatedly presenting herself as a lawyer without a licence.

Campaign for Accountability said Zacharia had described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative non-profit organisation.
"Ms. Zacharia has represented herself as a lawyer repeatedly to buttress her reputation and credibility," said the group's executive director, Michelle Kuppersmith.
"The State Bar should investigate whether Ms. Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials," she added.
Trump described Zacharia as "an attorney" when announcing her appointment on Friday, but journalists have found no record of her being licensed to practise law in any US state.
"I practised international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials," Zacharia said in a statement to AFP, without clarifying whether she held a US law licence.
Zacharia has not specified where, if anywhere, she was admitted to the bar. Asked by reporters on Tuesday where she had passed the bar exam, Zacharia replied: "When I moved to China."
California's state bar confirmed to US media that it had no record of Zacharia holding a licence under either her married or maiden name.
Zacharia, 41, graduated from Pepperdine University's law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practise law.
Foreign nationals cannot sit China's bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms.
Zacharia previously worked for a law firm in Beijing, according to her professional profile.
The controversy followed a rocky first appearance as White House press secretary on Tuesday, when Zacharia read extensively from prepared notes during a briefing lasting just 14 minutes.
She took questions from only three news organisations, all considered sympathetic to Trump, and stumbled over some answers, at one point accidentally referring to the president as her husband.
Her performance drew criticism from former White House press secretary Jen Psaki, now a TV news host, who compared it to a "Saturday Night Live" comedy sketch.
Trump, however, praised Zacharia's debut, telling reporters: "I thought she was very good."
Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public defenders of Trump's second administration.

83c067a1175ec72a: BULLHEAD CITY: US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that he wanted to see Pope Leo XIV "get well" after the pontiff underwent surgery in Rome this week to remove a cancerous tumour.

4a220b1e35c92a38: MILAN: Serie A clubs set an unwelcome record on Wednesday as two defeats ensured that all four Italian teams lost on the same Champions League match day for the first time in history.

AS Roma were beaten 4-3 at home by Real Madrid and debutants Como lost 3-2 to Feyenoord in Rotterdam. On Tuesday, Inter Milan went down 4-3 at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, and Napoli succumbed to a 3-1 defeat at Villarreal.

For Serie A champions Inter, the home setback against Brugge highlighted a stark decline in form. Inter have now lost seven of their last eight Champions League games, a far cry from the side that reached the final in 2023 and 2025.

Italian football is in a transitional period following the national team's failure to qualify for the World Cup for a third consecutive tournament. The Italian Football Federation is under the temporary stewardship of special administrator Giovanni Malago after he resigned as president this month.

Roma looked on course for a famous victory over record 15-times European champions Real as they led 3-1 after a Donyell Malen double. The Italians, however, conceded three goals in the final seven minutes with former Roma defender Antonio Rudiger delivering Madrid's 90th-minute winner.

"It has to be a valuable lesson, we need to be fully focused for the full 90 minutes plus stoppages. I think it has to be an issue of mentality, because when you concede three practically identical goals in seven minutes, something is wrong," Roma forward Matias Soule told Amazon Prime.
Como manager Cesc Fabregas admitted the elite European competition comes with a steep learning curve after his side suffered a narrow defeat at Feyenoord.

"The Champions League is the strongest competition. There is a higher level here than at a World Cup," Fabregas said. "It is a gift for this club and I will keep saying it. We will get there step by step, we have a path to follow. We need to keep cool heads and be consistent."
