21ac63ec92794373: PETALING JAYA: You spot an investment opportunity online. The company looks promising, the pitch is slick and, perhaps most reassuringly, hundreds of other people have already put their money in.

But does that make it a better investment? Not necessarily, although new Malaysian research suggests the behaviour of other investors can strongly influence whether an equity crowdfunding campaign succeeds.
Research presented at the National Financial Literacy Symposium in Kuala Lumpur on Oct 7 analysed 335 campaigns hosted on three licensed Malaysian equity crowdfunding platforms.
The study, led by Xiamen University Malaysia assistant professor You Hui Wei, examined the signals investors appear to rely on when deciding whether to back young businesses.

Of the factors studied, “social-proof cues, particularly the number of investors” emerged as the strongest predictors of campaign success. Disclosure of a company’s valuation was another important factor, while younger firms were also associated with a higher likelihood of reaching their fundraising targets.

Social proof refers to the tendency to look at what others are doing when making an uncertain decision. A busy restaurant can seem more appealing than an empty one; a product bought by thousands of people may feel safer than one nobody has tried

Startup investing is obviously more complicated, but similar behaviour can come into play. Potential investors generally have far less information about an early-stage company than its founders do, and unlike a large listed company, a startup may have little operating history, limited financial information and no analyst coverage.

In that situation, visible clues - including how many other people have invested - can become more influential. The researchers said financial-literacy efforts should help investors interpret “a small set of high-impact signals” rather than simply assume those signals indicate a sound investment.

A growing investor count may attract still more people, although that does not necessarily mean the crowd itself caused a campaign to succeed. A strong business may simply have convinced many investors independently, with the rising number of backers then providing additional reassurance to others.
What are Malaysians investing in?

Equity crowdfunding (ECF) allows startups and smaller businesses to raise money online from multiple investors. Unlike donating to a crowdfunding campaign or pre-ordering a product, an ECF investor receives shares in the business and becomes a shareholder.
According to the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC), more than 22,000 investors had participated in ECF since its introduction, while 1,979 invested in 2025 alone.
Some 71.5% of those who participated that year were first-time ECF investors, while retail investors made up 59% of participants and Malaysians accounted for 98% of all investors.

For smaller investors, accessibility is part of the attraction. Rather than needing large amounts of capital to back a private company, ECF platforms allow individuals to participate with comparatively modest sums, although that accessibility should not be mistaken for safety.

That distinction is particularly important when interpreting the new research. The study looked at whether campaigns successfully raised their targeted amount, but it did not examine whether those companies subsequently grew, paid dividends or delivered profitable exits for their investors.

A startup that hits its fundraising goal has therefore succeeded at raising money - not necessarily at making money for shareholders. The SC puts the risk plainly: “Investing in start-ups and early-stage businesses involves high risks.”

Among those risks are losing the entire investment, difficulty selling shares, receiving no dividends and seeing an ownership stake diluted if the company later issues more shares. Under current limits, retail investors may invest up to RM5,000 in a single ECF issuer and no more than RM50,000 across ECF investments within a 12-month period.
The commission also advises investors to study the company, its finances, how it intends to use the money raised and the risks involved before committing funds.

That advice sits neatly alongside the new research because seeing hundreds of people backing a startup tells you something: the campaign has generated interest and convinced others to put money behind it. What it cannot tell you is whether those people are right.
When it comes to startup investing, the crowd may help explain where the money is going, but it remains no substitute for understanding what you are actually buying.
1b23bb0cff29eaa1: PETALING JAYA: PAS may be fast‑tracking its ambitions for federal leadership, viewing its cooperation with Umno as the party’s best chance of leading Putrajaya, according to a political analyst.
Akademi Nusantara’s Azmi Hassan said PAS recognises that, on its own, it would struggle to build the nationwide influence and support needed to form the federal government, even in the long term.
He said Umno enjoys broader appeal across Malaysia, while PAS’s strength is concentrated in Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu.
Azmi said PAS’s current partnership with Umno was not simply about political survival but about positioning itself closer to federal power.
“I don’t think PAS is prepared to wait another 10 years to be part of the federal government or to see one of its MPs appointed prime minister.
“I don’t think that is the intention behind its current cooperation with Umno,” he told FMT.
Azmi said PAS may be willing to defer to Umno for now, though a swift shift in tone may occur if the outcome of the next general election (GE16) favours the Islamic party.
"Playing second fiddle now is just to ride on Umno's popularity," he said. "But if they have the greater number of seats, PAS will push for the prime minister's post."
According to Azmi, the Perikatan Nasional coalition may be turning into a “thing of the past” for PAS, though the party may continue working with Hamzah Zainudin's Wawasan.
Last week, former Umno information chief Shahril Hamdan suggested that PAS may be prepared to wait between five and 10 years before mounting a serious push for national leadership.

He said Umno seems more focused on regaining power immediately, while PAS may prefer to use its time in government to build administrative experience and increase familiarity among voters and civil servants with the party.

Another analyst, Mazlan Ali of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia, agreed with Shahril, noting that PAS was aware of its shortcomings when compared to Umno, particularly its lack of prominent figures and experience in federal administration.
He said Umno, which governed Malaysia from independence until 2018, has decades of experience that PAS can learn from.
"PAS faces the limitation of being perceived as a local party with appeal primarily among traditionalist Malays.
“It needs more time to learn from Umno’s experience in the federal government before it is truly ready to take over the reins of power itself in the future," he said.
Mazlan expects PAS to allow Umno to lead Putrajaya if the two parties succeed in forming a government after GE16.
However, he cautioned that such a move could backfire on PAS, while potentially aiding Umno's bid to regain support among Malay voters.

“A major risk for PAS is that if Umno manages to regain the trust of the Malays, as it did in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s, PAS could lose its influence, given that the two parties compete for the same segment of Malay voters," he said.
Mazlan said PAS and Umno were ultimately political rivals, and that any gains achieved through cooperation could eventually result in renewed competition.
An alliance could strengthen both parties and improve their chances of winning GE16, he said, but its long-term success would depend on whether they are able to maintain ties.
“If the relationship between the two parties is not further strengthened, they may well return to competing against each other on the political stage for the Malay vote in the future,” he said.
0a81eccd644875c6: PETALING JAYA: PAS mungkin sedang mempercepatkan usaha mencapai cita-citanya untuk menerajui kerajaan persekutuan, dengan melihat kerjasama Umno sebagai peluang terbaik parti itu memimpin Putrajaya, menurut seorang penganalisis politik.

Azmi Hassan daripada Akademi Nusantara berkata, PAS sedar ia akan menghadapi kesukaran untuk membina pengaruh dan sokongan di seluruh negara yang diperlukan bagi membentuk kerajaan persekutuan jika bergerak secara bersendirian, walaupun dalam jangka panjang.
Katanya, Umno mempunyai tarikan lebih luas di seluruh Malaysia, manakala kekuatan PAS tertumpu di Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan dan Terengganu.
Menurutnya, kerjasama PAS dengan Umno ketika ini bukan sekadar untuk kelangsungan politik, sebaliknya bertujuan meletakkan parti itu lebih hampir kepada kuasa di peringkat persekutuan.
“Saya tidak fikir PAS sanggup menunggu 10 tahun lagi untuk menjadi sebahagian daripada kerajaan persekutuan atau melihat salah seorang Ahli Parlimennya dilantik sebagai perdana menteri.
“Saya tidak fikir itu tujuan di sebalik kerjasama dengan Umno ketika ini,” katanya kepada FMT.
Azmi berkata, PAS mungkin bersedia untuk memainkan peranan kedua selepas Umno buat masa ini, namun perubahan pendirian boleh berlaku dengan pantas jika keputusan PRU16 memihak kepada parti Islam itu.
“Buat masa ini, memainkan peranan kedua hanyalah untuk menumpang populariti Umno. Tetapi jika mereka memperoleh jumlah kerusi yang lebih banyak, PAS akan menuntut jawatan perdana menteri,” katanya.
Menurut Azmi, gabungan Perikatan Nasional (PN) mungkin semakin menjadi 'sejarah' bagi PAS, meskipun parti itu mungkin terus bekerjasama dengan Wawasan pimpinan Hamzah Zainudin.
Minggu lalu, bekas ketua penerangan Umno, Shahril Hamdan, berkata PAS mungkin sedia menunggu antara lima hingga 10 tahun lagi sebelum melancarkan usaha serius untuk menerajui kepimpinan negara.

Beliau berkata, Umno kelihatan lebih fokus mendapatkan semula kuasa dengan segera, manakala PAS mungkin lebih memilih menggunakan tempohnya dalam kerajaan bagi membina pengalaman pentadbiran serta beri masa kepada pengundi dan penjawat awam untuk mengenali parti itu.

Seorang lagi penganalisis, Mazlan Ali daripada Universiti Teknologi Malaysia, bersetuju dengan Shahril dan berkata PAS menyedari kelemahannya berbanding Umno, khususnya dari segi kekurangan tokoh terkemuka dan pengalaman dalam pentadbiran persekutuan.
Beliau berkata, Umno yang mentadbir Malaysia sejak kemerdekaan sehingga 2018, mempunyai pengalaman selama berdekad yang boleh dipelajari PAS.
“PAS berdepan kekangan kerana dianggap sebagai parti tempatan yang daya tarikannya hanya tertumpu dalam kalangan orang Melayu tradisionalis.
“PAS memerlukan lebih banyak masa untuk mempelajari pengalaman Umno dalam kerajaan persekutuan sebelum benar-benar bersedia untuk mengambil alih tampuk kuasa sendiri pada masa hadapan,” katanya.
Mazlan menjangkakan, PAS mungkin membenarkan Umno menerajui Putrajaya jika kedua-dua parti berjaya membentuk kerajaan selepas PRU16.
Bagaimanapun, beliau memberi amaran langkah PAS itu boleh memakan diri, selain berpotensi membantu usaha Umno mendapatkan semula sokongan dalam kalangan pengundi Melayu.
“Risiko besar bagi PAS ialah jika Umno berjaya mendapatkan semula kepercayaan orang Melayu, seperti dilakukannya pada 1970-an, 1980-an dan 1990-an.
"PAS boleh kehilangan pengaruhnya memandangkan kedua-dua parti itu bersaing untuk segmen pengundi Melayu yang sama,” katanya.
Mazlan berkata, PAS dan Umno adalah pesaing politik, dan sebarang keuntungan yang dicapai melalui kerjasama boleh membawa kepada persaingan semula pada masa hadapan.
Beliau berkata, pakatan boleh mengukuhkan kedua-dua parti dan meningkatkan peluang memenangi PRU16, tetapi kejayaan jangka panjangnya bergantung pada keupayaan mengekalkan hubungan tersebut.
“Jika hubungan antara kedua-dua parti itu tidak diperkukuh lagi, mereka mungkin kembali bersaing antara satu sama lain di pentas politik untuk mendapatkan undi Melayu pada masa hadapan,” katanya.
16fb9b6ca4d78554: BRASILIA: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's party will file a complaint against tech giant Meta before the Organization of American States (OAS), alleging election "interference," his campaign reported Wednesday.
The leftist leader is seeking a fourth nonconsecutive term in an Oct 25 runoff, where he will face Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro.
His party maintains that Meta is harming his campaign by restricting his online content, which the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram denies.
"It's time to denounce (Meta) before the international community, starting with the OAS," party communications secretary Eden Valadares told reporters, adding that Lula himself had ordered the move.

His campaign earlier claimed that Meta in recent days "prevented President Lula's profile from promoting Instagram feed posts," while a post from his official account "experienced an interruption in view counts, which affected its reach."

It also said that prior to last Sunday's first round of voting, in which Flavio Bolsonaro finished first, the profiles of Lula and other leftist leaders "suddenly disappeared from Instagram's search function".
Meta's Brazil office denied the charges, calling them "simply false" and "not supported by the facts".
The incumbent's campaign called a Thursday meeting with international election observers to discuss the alleged interference.
Lula has claimed that the United States is trying to interfere in the elections in favor of Flavio Bolsonaro, whose father is an ally of US President Donald Trump.
Following the first round of voting, Lula -- who does not use a mobile phone -- launched a social media push that includes videos of him addressing his online followers.
8fa24f1c8d5e1710: SAN ISIDRO, (Argentina): Diego Maradona's family on Wednesday called for his medical team to be given stiff prison terms over what two of his daughters called his "murder."
Seven medical professionals have been on trial since April over Maradona's death on November 25, 2020, while convalescing after surgery for a brain clot.
The star of the 1986 World Cup died aged 60 of heart failure and acute pulmonary edema, two weeks after going under the knife.
His medical team is accused of providing grossly inadequate care in the lead-up to his death at a private home rented for his convalescence.
Maradona's family are divided on the severity of the punishment they believe his carers should face.
A lawyer for two of his daughters, Dalma and Gianinna, on Wednesday accused his carers of "murder" and asked that six of the seven accused be sentenced to up to 15 years in prison.
"They killed a mythological hero," lawyer Fernando Burlando said, accusing the defendants of "brutal indifference" to the icon's fate.
Counsel for the champion's three sisters Rita, Claudia and Ana, sought terms of up to 10 years for five of the seven defendants.
Their lawyer Pablo Jurado called for medical coordinator Nancy Forlini to receive the harshest punishment.
On Tuesday, a lawyer for Maradona's youngest son, 13-year-old Diego Fernando Maradona, had called for the player's personal physician Leopoldo Luque and Forlini to be each given 16-year sentences.
State prosecutors kicked off the closing arguments last week with a call for guilty findings against six of the seven accused and prison sentences ranging from four to 12 years.
They added that Luque should receive the stiffest punishment.
The closing arguments are set to continue until the end of October.s

a8731c475a99d145: WASHINGTON: The White House was facing mounting questions Wednesday over new press secretary Katie Zacharia's legal credentials, after a faltering first day in the job when she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam.

A US watchdog group filed a complaint with the State Bar of California, asking it to investigate whether President Donald Trump's spokeswoman -- the public face of the administration -- had broken the law by repeatedly presenting herself as a lawyer without a license.
Campaign for Accountability said Zacharia had described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.
"Ms. Zacharia has represented herself as a lawyer repeatedly to buttress her reputation and credibility," said the group's executive director, Michelle Kuppersmith.
"The State Bar should investigate whether Ms. Zacharia has misled the public about her credentials," she added.
Trump described Zacharia as "an attorney" when announcing her appointment Friday, but journalists have found no record of her being licensed to practice law in any US state.
"I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials," Zacharia said in a statement to AFP, without clarifying whether she held a US law license.
Zacharia has not specified where, if anywhere, she was admitted to the bar. Asked by reporters Tuesday where she had passed the bar exam, Zacharia replied: "When I moved to China."
California's state bar confirmed to US media that it had no record of Zacharia holding a license under either her married or maiden name.
Zacharia, 41, graduated from Pepperdine University's law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law.
Foreign nationals cannot sit China's bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms.
Zacharia previously worked for a law firm in Beijing, according to her professional profile.
The controversy followed a rocky first appearance as White House press secretary on Tuesday, when Zacharia read extensively from prepared notes during a briefing lasting just 14 minutes.
She took questions from only three news organizations, all considered sympathetic to Trump, and stumbled over some answers, at one point accidentally referring to the president as her husband.
Her performance drew criticism from former White House press secretary Jen Psaki, now a TV news host, who compared it to a "Saturday Night Live" comedy sketch.
Trump, however, praised Zacharia's debut, telling reporters: "I thought she was very good."
Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down in August after becoming one of the most prominent public defenders of Trump's second administration.

e279dd9efad93ec8: KUALA LUMPUR: The Defence Ministry is strengthening its commitment to the welfare and future of armed forces personnel and veterans through the MyBakat Veteran initiative, which aims to benefit more than 15,000 people by 2030.

Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the initiative underscores the ministry's new approach to ensuring that personnel receive support not only during their service but are also better prepared to pursue a second career after retirement.
He said the ministry is placing greater emphasis on aligning military skills and experience with industry requirements to broaden job opportunities for its personnel and veterans.

"We are moving away from the 'train first, find a job later' approach towards directly matching personnel's competencies with industry needs, relevant training and actual career opportunities," he said at the signing of a Note of Cooperation between the ministry and the Human Resources Ministry to implement MyBakat Veteran yesterday.

Defence secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali and human resources secretary-general Datuk Azman Mohd Yusof signed the Note of Cooperation in the presence of Khaled and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
Also present was Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.

A memorandum of understanding (MoU) was also signed by MINDEF, the Armed Forces Ex-Servicemen Affairs Corporation (Perhebat) and the Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) to facilitate the placement of Perhebat trainees and veterans with companies under MEF for a six-month transition period before they are absorbed into permanent positions.
Khaled said the initiative focuses on career preparation at least two years before retirement, noting that between 5,000 and 7,000 armed forces personnel leave the service each year.

"The strategic collaboration also offers opportunities for military experience and expertise to be recognised as professional qualifications through the Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) and Malaysian Skills Diploma (DKM), subject to competency assessments and eligibility criteria.

"It also strengthens the roles of Perhebat and the Malaysian Armed Forces Veterans Affairs Department (JHEV), with support from TalentCorp and relevant agencies, in providing career transition training and access to job opportunities," he said.
He said the collaboration highlights the ministry's efforts to expand the support ecosystem for military personnel through a more structured, integrated approach that responds to labour market needs.
b442852f363fda15: MEXICO CITY: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she will sign a presidential decree on Wednesday requiring digital platforms, including social media and streaming sites, to shield children and teenagers from violent, sexual and other harmful content.

The decree, which will step up scrutiny of big technology companies in Latin America's second-largest economy, comes after an attack by two 18-year-old former students on a high school in the northern state of Coahuila in early October left one person dead and wounded three others.
Digital platforms will have one month to come into compliance with the decree, government adviser Luisa Maria Alcalde said.
Sheinbaum added that if companies failed to follow the decree, the government would back a bill to penalise the platforms.
Officials said they had already met with representatives of Meta, Microsoft, Apple, TikTok, Google, X and Huawei to discuss the matter.

A Meta spokesman told Reuters that the company, which runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Threads, is "aware of the decree" and that it will "analyse it in detail", adding that it has long had tools in place to help parents "guide their children's digital experience”.

"We will continue to engage with the authorities to help create a safer digital environment for teenagers in the country,” the spokesman said, adding that Meta offers safety features on its platforms which include safeguards to limit who can make contact with children, as well as the monitoring of viewed content.
Microsoft, Apple, TikTok, Google, X and Huawei did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

Mexico's move follows a broader global push to protect minors online, with governments in Europe and Australia tightening oversight of digital platforms and US states pursuing a range of child-safety measures.
Brazil has also moved to strengthen protections for children online. Such measures have raised questions over how to protect minors while safeguarding privacy and freedom of expression.

b6c0bd4fad2da1b1: PARIS: Football's world governing body Fifa is planning to set up a US$6.35-billion development fund for the next four years, AFP learned Wednesday from a source close to the matter.
The plan is due to be approved at its Council meeting on Thursday in Zurich, where Fifa president Gianni Infantino and the 36 other members of the federation's executive will gather.

To finance this development fund for the 2026–2030 period, which would allow money to be distributed to Fifa's 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations, it would draw in part on its financial reserves after a commercially successful 2026 World Cup.
The plan, first revealed by the Associated Press, would allow for the payment of US$25 million to each of its 211 member federations.

This is far more than the US$10 million called for by two of Infantino's chief critics, Aleksander Ceferin, the boss of the European confederation Uefa, and Victor Montagliani, the head of Concacaf, the confederation of North and Central America and the Caribbean.

Thursday's gathering is the first such meeting since April 28, and comes amid a crisis in the governance of world football, following Infantino's announcement this summer of his desire to open Fifa's premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.
That plan was ultimately abandoned in the face of widespread criticism from the football world, with a rebellion led by Uefa, Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

At the end of September, Infantino launched a consultation process with the federations to reform how the global body operates, announcing that the first proposals could be examined as early as Thursday's Council meeting.
The 56-year-old, who has headed Fifa since 2016, is running for re-election in March 2027.
His opponents have so far failed to agree on a candidate.
Ceferin has chosen to stand for a new term at the helm of Uefa and, according to several media outlets, Montagliani is expected to do the same at Concacaf.
The deadline for submitting candidacies is Nov 18.

54f95897dfd35ce6: Dalam artikel ini saya ingin mengulas tulisan sahabat saya A Kathirasen berjudul Poets, Philosophers and Policy: The moral language of Budget 2027, yang mengupas bahasa falsafah, puisi dan agama dalam belanjawan Anwar Ibrahim. Mesej artikel tersebut adalah bacaan penulis sendiri betapa Anwar cuba memberi suatu mesej ‘kemanusiaan sejagat’ dalam terjemahan fiskal dan angka-angka wang ringgit dalam alokasi-alokasi masing-masing.

Kathirasen ingin menarik perhatian kepada asas bahawa belanjawan adalah aspek kematangan kemanusiaan, bukan semata-mata wang kocek di sini dan sana untuk dihabiskan. Penulis veteran itu juga ingin mengkiaskan usaha Anwar untuk mensejagatkan isu keperluan daripada pengasingan perkauman. Dalam artikel ini saya akan memanjangkan tafsiran Kathirasen dengan membawa mesej saya sendiri, iaitu, bahasa dan rujukan yang digunakan membawa konsep pemerintahan dan penjagaan negara memerlukan suatu bahasa Melayu-global.

Ada dua aspek yang ingin saya sentuh tentang penggunaan rujukan pelbagai kaum dan agama serta pelbagai sumber ketamadunan manusia dari kitab suci agama, kepada falsafah pemikir dan puisi pujangga. Pertama adalah tuduhan ‘liberal’ kepada sesiapa Melayu Muslim yang menggunakan sumber pemikiran atau falsafah dan refleksi spiritual daripada selain sumber Islam.
Keduanya adalah apakah yang saya maksudkan sebagai bahasa lingua franca Melayu global sebagai hamparan kepada pemikiran Anwar sebagai intelek Melayu-Islam.

Yang pertama adalah tuduhan yang selalu diajukan kepada sesiapa yang membawa argumen atau perbahasan atau konsep daripada pemikiran, refleksi dan falsafah dari selain Islam Sunni akan membawa tuduhan ‘liberal’ dan merosakkan serta menyesatkan orang Islam. Sebagai seorang ilmuan seni bina, saya amat memahami keperluan menggunakan sumber-sumber konsep, pemikiran dan prinsip-prinsip seni bina dari Barat seperti pemikiran Frank Lloyd Wright, Louis Sullivan, William Morris, Walter Gropius, Mies van der Rohe dan Le Corbusier. Sumber-sumber falsafah dan pemikiran dari Amerika Syarikat, England, Perancis dan Jerman amat perlu saya garapkan dalam memikir semula teori atau prinsip seni bina Islam, seni bina Malaysia dan seni bina Melayu moden.

Peminjaman pemikiran dari sumber luar atau lain dari kaum dan agama kita sendiri bukan bermaksud mengagungkan atau mengkiblatkan Barat atau Timur tetapi memberi pengiktirafan bahawa bangsa-bangsa manusia yang lain melalui pemodenan dan kesedaran dalam tahap yang berbeza serta waktu yang lebih awal dari kita di Malaysia. Arus revolusi industri meranapkan hubungan masyarakat dan pemerintah serta pemikiran ‘enlightenment’ pula mencabar tafsiran kehidupan, kosmos dan geografi duni daripada hanya interpretasi gereja sahaja.

Negara kita di rantau ini, walaupun mempunyai segala macam telefon pintar, AI, serta teknologi baharu yang terkini masih melalui suatu pertembungan antara pemikiran sains, politik dan agama yang telah dilalui orang di Barat dunia lebih 200 tahun sebelumnya.

Kita Melayu sampai lewat sikit. Maka itu penggunaan serta peminjaman konsep, istilah dan pemikiran daripada selain Islam menggambarkan keupayaan seorang Melayu menggarap dan membentuk suatu belanjawan yang bernyawakan moral, wawasan jauh dan ketamadunan kemanusiaan.

Belanjawan negara adalah bukan semata-mata belanjawan korporat yang tahu untung rugi sahaja. Maka itu adalah tidak wajar pada sesiapa yang akan menuding jari “nah itu bunyi orang Melayu-Islam liberal” ataupun “nah itu bunyi orang yang dijajah pemikiran kolonial dari Barat dan dari sumber musuh Islam”.

Sebagai ilmuan, semua para cerdik pandai tahu bahawa kebenaran merentasi kaum dan agama kerana kaum dan agama yang difahami itu telah disempitkan oleh golongan yang disuruh menjaga integriti warisan tersebut. Namun demikian, penjaga warisan ugama yang berpendidikan tidak pelbagai disiplin dan ilmu hanya dapat melihatnya dengan satu belah teropong sahaja.

Perkara kedua adalah bagaimana Anwar memainkan peranan seorang Melayu global dan bukan Melayu-parti atau Melayu-ustaz. Untuk menjadi suatu bangsa yang berjaya, orang Melayu perlu mengetahui pelbagai sumber pemikiran yang datang dari pelbagai bangsa dan budaya. Seperti juga Hang Tuah yang telah memohon ayahandanya untuk beliau mempelajari lebih daripada 10 bahasa asing. Melayu yang mempunyai akses kepada pemikiran daripadapelbagai sumber lain tidak akan terbantut kepada retorik perpaduan Melayu untuk kuasa serta kesucuan agama tanpa kematangan global dan menyeluruh. Saya sering mengajar pelajar PhD bahawa semua ilmu adalah tafsiran orang yang hendak menggunakannya pada ketika itu dan dalam konteks kefahaman teknologi, sains dan budaya manusia selainnya sahaja. Maka, sesuatu ilmu seperti ilmu agama boleh diperluaskan atau diperkecilkan mengikut kehendak seseorang. Ilmu perlu melimpah kepada pemikiran dan tafsiran setiap masa berubah dan juga perubahan untuk berpindah kerana situasi semasa.

Akhir sekali, saya mencadangkan janganlah kita terlalu pantas menghukum ‘sesat’ atau ‘liberal’ kepada sesiapa hanya kerana mereka menggunakan istilah luar yang kita sendiri tidak tahu hujung pangkal. Perkara pokok yang perlu dijiwai daripada artikel saya dan Kathirasen adalah belanjawan bukan semata-mata angka yang diagih-agihkan kepada semua kememterian. Seperkara lagi adalah penggunaan istilah, konsep dan falsafah yang merentasi jurang kaum, agama dan budaya adalah keupayaan berfikir luar daripada kepompong tradisi. Hanya dengan percampuran dan menjunamkan diri ke dalam budaya lain maka barulah kita boleh menggarap solusi baharu serta arah tuju sama yang cekal dan kental.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
4b2957f67a3ef1ea: KUALA LUMPUR: Simulation racing, or sim racing, may be a relatively niche sport in Malaysia, but one young enthusiast is determined to help steer it into the spotlight.

Sim racing is a form of virtual motorsport that uses realistic racing games and specialised equipment, such as steering wheels and pedals, to recreate the experience of driving on an actual racetrack.
As the sport gains traction internationally, Malaysian sim racer Dhanesh Wigneswaran hopes to nurture the next generation of local talent through his DannyR Esports Studio in Subang Jaya.
And he is leading by example. This December, the 26-year-old will compete in the Gran Turismo World Series (GTWS) 2026 World Finals in Tokyo as the only racer from Southeast Asia.

“It’s been an amazing experience so far. There are some very nice and professional racing setups in the World Series, and they’ve really created a conducive and comfortable environment here,” Dhanesh told FMT Lifestyle.
“The vibes have also been great. It’s been wonderful getting to meet some of the top sim racers in the world, learning from them and hanging out with them.”

Dhanesh is already well established in the local Gran Turismo scene, with achievements including championship titles at the Unleashed Youth Sim Racing and GT7 Malaysia Esports League competitions last year.

He is currently representing Volkswagen in the Manufacturers Cup, in which sim racers compete on behalf of major car brands. Drivers race virtual versions of their respective manufacturers’ cars, earning points throughout the series.

The competition begins with six online rounds to determine the 12 manufacturers that advance, followed by live rounds in Milan, Tokyo and Singapore. The season culminates in the world finals in Tokyo.
This is Dhanesh’s second appearance at a World Series Finals, having previously represented Malaysia in the Nations Cup in 2023.

“I enjoy driving with Volkswagen because their car, the Beetle Gr.3, has very good acceleration and fuel consumption. It also sticks well to the road when we take high-speed corners. It’s very balanced overall,” he said.

Dhanesh’s road to the Tokyo finals began with the GTWS Online Series in January, where he emerged as Volkswagen’s highest-scoring driver in the Asia-Oceania region and helped the manufacturer finish 11th overall.
He later faced a setback in the second live round in Tokyo, finishing 12th after his car struggled in adverse weather conditions.
Undeterred, Dhanesh is aiming to bounce back when he returns for the finals, where he hopes to score as many points as possible for Volkswagen and help secure a top-six finish.

“The sport is actually a major mental game: the important thing is to stay focused. It’s easy to see the track and all the big names participating and get intimidated, but you can’t do that,” he said.
“I always remember is that if I can do it in training, I can do it in the real event as well.”
Although Japanese drivers dominate much of the Asia-Oceania field, Dhanesh said he didn't encounter many difficulties competing alongside them.

Language can occasionally be a barrier because of his limited Japanese, but most of his fellow racers have been friendly and welcoming. And while they may be fierce rivals on the virtual racetrack, many have become good friends away from it.
While he prepares for December with almost daily practice sessions, Dhanesh is also devoting time to developing potential new racers.
He believes interest in the sport has grown following the recent Citrawarna Speed Festival 2026 in Putrajaya, which featured a large-scale racing simulator competition.

“I’m very impressed at the level of sim-racing talent I’m seeing now in Malaysia. You have many fast up-and-coming sim racers who are performing well at home, and I believe they can perform very well in live events,” Dhanesh said.
“I hope the sport enjoys more attention soon. It’s great fun with great prizes, and it’s the best way to get introduced to real car racing.”
Learn more about DannyR Esports Studio on Instagram.
cef6d0807cbc1074: The Budget 2027 allocation for the health ministry (MOH) and public healthcare has been raised to RM47.7bil, only RM1.2 billion extra which is the smallest increase in five years.
This falls well short of the Pakatan Harapan election promise to target 5% of GDP for public sector health expenditure in terms of both money and percentage.
At 10.3% of the total federal budget and 2.1% of GDP, the budget for the MOH has hardly changed in the last five years.

This shows that it is still “business as usual” in terms of public sector health expenditure and the small increase in the ministry’s budget barely exceeds the general inflation rate let alone medical inflation.

The government has met its longstanding promise to solve the issue of contract doctors and must be given credit for that. Anwar claims that MOH will create more than 9,000 vacancies to absorb the current contract doctors and newly trained housemen.
The allocation for the number of positions shows this, and the promise that new batches of trained housemen will be appointed directly to permanent positions is likely to be kept.

This demonstrates that coordination with the public service department (JPA) and the political will to solve the position problem through planning can be effective. It has taken more than a decade, but better late than never.
The new medical officers looking to serve in the public sector are still looking for higher pay, flexibility in appointments and job security.

The increase to the incentives for nurses and paramedics is only RM100 per month and does little to address concerns about low pay compared to peers in the private sector and overseas, such as in Singapore and the Middle East.
Brain drain is considered severe; this budget policy announcement is only a small, welcome adjustment and does not address the systemic issue of staff retention.
The realisation that more ambulances are needed for effective emergency care and the decision to purchase additional ambulances is a welcome change in management.
Nonetheless, there still are too many gaps in the public healthcare system.
With this small budget increase and without complementary policies and the necessary political will, these issues will not be resolved.
Some of these issues are not about money at all. They are about management and changing old-style human resource processes.

On the other hand, spending for public-private healthcare has increased from RM144 million to RM200 million for next year. This is a substantial increase for the outsourcing of public sector patients to the private sector.

An earlier government report stated that RM66.5 million was spent on 24,000 outsourced patients. If the government can maintain this rate, it could free up more than 70,000 public sector patients next year.
While this would improve waiting times in public hospitals, it would probably have only a minimal impact compared to the estimated 19 million outpatient visits in 2024.
However, for certain medical treatments and procedures, this could have a meaningful impact on waiting times.
With the Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme now covering 14 specialty areas, the increase in allocation will be welcome news for public sector patients but it is a form of privatisation.

The policy announcement regarding MediAsas and price transparency in private healthcare is also a form of privatisation and likely to have a greater impact on access to care and help to keep medical inflation in check.
While these might not require significant budget allocation from the government, the government will certainly need to step up its regulatory efforts.
This is the real challenge. If healthcare is to be balanced between public and private providers, then regulation and management must improve.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.

fc7c7d8e2be54e0a: Cisco “strongly” implored customers to patch yet another critical, make-me-root vulnerability in its Secure Email Gateway (SEG), one that has already been exploited in zero-day attacks. A Cisco spokesperson told The Register that the critical vuln, which received a 9.8 out of 10 CVSS rating, affects “a limited number of customers.” The bug, now tracked as CVE‑2026‑76519, allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to write files and execute commands with root privileges on the appliance’s operating system - simply by sending a malicious email. In separate Wednesday advisories, both the networking vendor and the US government warned that attackers were exploiting the latest SEG vulnerability before Cisco issued a fix. The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and set a Saturday deadline for federal agencies to fix the issue. “We are aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability,” the spokesperson said, but declined to answer our questions about how many appliances had been compromised, and what attackers were doing with this access after exploiting the bug. “We strongly urge customers to upgrade to a fixed software release and follow additional recommendations and hardening guidance in our advisory,” the spokesperson said. The flaw exists in SEG’s Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature, and it’s due to improper handling of email attachments. An attacker could exploit the bug by sending an email with a malicious attachment, and a successful exploit would allow them to write files and execute commands as root on the compromised appliance. This vulnerability affects both physical and virtual SEG appliances running a vulnerable release of Cisco AsyncOS Software if both of the following conditions are met: The File Reputation service, which is part of Cisco AMP, is enabled and assigned to a mail policy. The Content Scanner Tools version is earlier than 25.3.0.5525. Cisco's Wednesday advisory includes steps organizations can take to determine whether File Reputation is enabled and which Content Scanner Tools version is installed - so give that a read if you are unsure. Upgrading to a fixed Cisco AsyncOS Software release will patch the security hole, and there are no workarounds. The vendor recommends any customers who are running Cisco AsyncOS Software releases earlier than v 16.5 migrate to 16.5.0-780. In its alert, Cisco said it became aware of active exploitation in October. This is the second such zero-day in SEG in as many months. In mid-September, Cisco warned customers that criminals were exploiting a similar bug in SEG, tracked as CVE-2026-76461, that also turns a malicious email into root access. In January, attackers exploited another critical AsyncOS flaw, CVE-2025-20393, to break into Cisco SEG appliances and install persistence mechanisms. That bug eventually scored a perfect 10.®
9eb295a80fa64f4f: Earlier this week, a mass hack of refrigeration systems at an estimated 700 supermarkets throughout France caused them to suddenly malfunction, causing spoilage of untold tons of perishables and, in some cases, fires. As is now the norm, basic cybersecurity would have prevented it.

French authorities say the systems, made up of entire fleets of refrigerators and freezers throughout a store, were hacked. More specifically, Internet-connected controllers that allow technicians to remotely administer the store-wide systems were compromised. The unknown attackers responsible then activated defrosters long enough for the fridges to reach temperatures as high as 50° Celsius (122° Fahrenheit). By the time the mass compromise was discovered, food was spoiled, and in some cases their electrical systems caught fire.
The hacks that didn't have to happen

Multiple security advisories and public research reports show that all three of the controller models reportedly hacked in the incident—sold by Danfoss of Denmark and Dixell and its parent company Copeland in the US—contained critical vulnerabilities that allow attackers to remotely log in to the devices with the same system rights as administrators. Until recently, Danfoss controllers, for instance, used a credential that changes each day. The password is generated by the publicly available firmware based on the date. A hacker who takes the time to analyze the code can do the same thing on any device that hasn’t received a recent update. Daily passwords are identical across models located in hundreds or thousands of stores.

8df95ca30f9db531: A YouTuber who’s gained a following for trolling AI interview bots brought his own computing companion to an interview with him. As chaos ensued, viewers learned that having an AI as your interview agent isn't a good idea. Graham Dot Zip is a comedian whose YouTube channel has blown up recently thanks to videos of him demonstrating the absurdity of AI bots used to conduct early-stage interviews with job candidates. AI interviewers have become quite the phenomenon in recent months, and not one that job seekers are fond of, with plenty of videos and social media posts documenting hate for them. Enter Graham and his trolling of various interview bots. Some videos have garnered nearly 2 million views in the past few weeks. In one, he answers every question with gibberish responses that the AI parrots as if they’re cogent responses. In another, he has the bot gushing unnecessary pleasantries and thanks as the two go back and forth trying to be professionally polite. While it’s amusing to watch an AI try to deal with interviewees who are obviously trolling them, Graham’s most recent video is what really merits a mention here. In this instance, Graham pits his own AI representative, which he created to handle the interview for him, against an AI interviewer presented as acting on behalf of a company. Victor, Graham’s “representative,” misstates Graham’s qualifications and misrepresents his participation in a particular project. Then comes the kicker: When asked about salary expectations, Victor claims Graham would be happy to take the job for around $60,000 a year, which Graham vehemently disagrees with, saying he was looking at somewhere between $140K and $150K. The AI recruiter refuses to go above $90K. Graham steps out for a moment, and the two bots decide to schedule a follow-up interview without him. Upon his return, both are stuck in a loop thanking each other for their time and saying goodbye, seemingly without the ability to terminate the call. While funny, there’s a bit of a dystopian nightmare to be found here, too. Although Graham may be trolling the AI interviewer, he's still been essentially cornered by his own AI bot’s poor ability to negotiate and refusal to listen to his instructions not to lie about his qualifications and his desired salary range. It’s a worrying prospect in the era of agentic commerce, where AI companies are trying to create AI agents that can shop for us and undertake other commercial exchanges. Who’s to say those bots are any better at negotiating for a good deal than Victor? If there’s anything to be learned from a growing number of videos of people trolling AI interview bots, convincing them they’re dying, and burning through those valuable AI tokens, it’s that, yet again, there are things AI is good for and things it’s not. Putting on a human mask and talking to human job candidates, frankly, isn’t something they ought to be doing - job seekers don’t think so, at least, despite AI HR departments seemingly becoming the norm. Given Victor’s poor negotiation skills, they probably shouldn’t be engaged in anything to do with trying to get consumers a deal, either. As the AI hellscape grows around us, with seemingly no limit to what a bot-pushing firm will try to sell, all we can do is laugh, it seems. Luckily, there are plenty of dumb bots out there ready to make AI providers and the companies using their services the butt of many an internet joke. ®

29ad242422527ec3: Despite previous controversies, it seems like the lords of Linux are warming to AI-assisted coding. The penguin's kernel community has agreed to stop asking coders to disclose whether they used bots to help with their contributions. And Linux kernel supremo Linus Torvalds has made clear that he opposes "stupid" AI disclosure rules as long as people understand the code they're submitting. "The Maintainers Summit reached consensus to deprecate the Assisted-by Tag," said Sasha Levin, a Linux kernel developer and engineer at Nvidia, in a message to the Linux kernel mailing list last week. "Remove the documentation requiring it." The policy had said that those using "any sort of advanced coding tool in the creation of [their] patch" should acknowledge that through the addition of an "Assisted-by" tag in the commit message. The AI labeling proposal initially took shape in July 2025. It became part of the documentation in January 2026. This was shortly after Torvalds said that he was fairly positive about vibe coding as a way for people to get into programming, but remained skeptical about its effect on software maintainability. Since then, he's warmed to AI tool usage. AI attribution wasn't an issue when the generated code was obvious, buggy, and bad. But in the past year or so, AI coding agents started producing code that is of acceptable quality for the purposes of the Linux kernel community. "LLMs are good enough now," said Greg Kroah-Hartman, a veteran Linux kernel maintainer, at the Linux Foundation's Open Source Summit in South Korea in August. "They've gotten good enough to find bugs because LLMs, AI, are just pattern matchers and code is nothing but patterns in a specific format." Cautious acceptance hasn't erased concerns about errors slipping through unnoticed, accountability, and coding agents reproducing copyrighted code. There's also still a stigma in some circles around the use of AI tools. Those who have spent years honing software skills, coding with limited assistance from tools, may disparage developers who don't understand the code they conjure with a prompt. Rapid change will do that – in the space of a few years, software production practices have changed drastically, and software quality, security, and maintenance practices have yet to fully adjust. The leading makers of AI coding agents – Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, and the like – are doing their best to promote AI-driven projects as better than anything a human developer could manage. Yet even they differ in their AI attribution practices. Claude adds provenance messages by default, but Codex does not. In fields such as advertising and art, content provenance can help assess misinformation and human creative input. For code, the focus tends to be more on functionality than form. In a prior discussion of the merits of the tag requirement, Jeff Layton, a Linux kernel developer with Red Hat, explained the rationale for reversing course. First, he said, not everyone abides by the policy. Second, he said, "it basically serves as free advertising for proprietary LLM companies." And third, he said, "it's not clear why we want to collect this info in the first place." Some kernel contributors still see value in the tagging requirement. "I'm not happy removing the tag without adding another mechanism for required disclosure," said Laurent Pinchart, a Linux kernel dev and founder of Ideas on Board, in a mailing list post on Tuesday. "Without that, I can foresee submitters pushing back on the question." Pinchart challenged the argument that AI labeling rules will just be ignored. "What this is about is setting our expectations, telling what we want and what we don't want," said Pinchart. "There's still value in that, and I'd argue there's even more value now. There will be people who won't care, there will be people who cheat. We've always had those, we'll keep having them, and we'll keep rejecting their contributions. I really don't get the unenforceable argument here." Linus Torvalds responded with an emphatic rejection of tool usage declarations. He wrote: What you are about is something entirely different. It has nothing to do with "expectations", and it has everything to do with your hangups. I don't understand this whole idiotic concept of "don't use AI for X". Here's a new rule just for you: don't use compilers for any of your kernel submissions. Because if you can't show that you really understand what the machine is actually doing by writing your code in assembler, then I don't want to see your code contribution. You clearly aren't competent if you can't write it that way. And btw, you had better not use an editor to write that commit message either. Because I need you to show me that you can actually write a good commit message without using tools that make it easy to backspace and hide the mistakes you made while typing. Ok? Because otherwise those tool-assisted commits of yours clearly aren't showing that you know what you are doing. Do you not see how UTTERLY STUPID those kinds of rules would be? So no. We're not going to make stupid rules that say "you can't use tools for X". The kind of expectations *I* have is that people do their best and I expect people to understand what they are doing. But that understanding has very little to do with what tools they use. And quite honestly, in my experience, the people I respect and call intelligent are not the ones that shy away from using new and interesting tools. ®

15182b3efcde6535: Researchers at security startup Xbow used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model to help chain three zero-day vulnerabilities in Chrome into an exploit capable of executing code outside the browser's sandbox on Windows machines. Xbow estimates that this could affect about one billion users worldwide. Google fixed all three, and paid the Xbow team a $250,000 bounty, its top reward for a Chrome full-chain exploit. The payout also proves a nice return on investment for the human bug hunters - Brendan Dolan-Gavitt, Andres Luksenberg, Baul Lee, and Willem Pinckaers - who spent just six days during the Black Hat and DEF CON conferences and about $40,000 in token charges to discover the vulnerabilities and build the attack chain. “The number on the check is impressive, but the time it took our team, with the help of a publicly available AI model, to break in is even more impressive,” Xbow CEO and founder Oege de Moor said on Tuesday. “A three letter intelligence-agency veteran told me that his team used to spend six months trying to identify this kind of vulnerability and get total access. We did it in six days.” In a separate technical writeup about the attack chain, Dolan-Gavitt detailed the work done by humans and AI agents. Agents, using OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol model, searched source code, tested the team’s hypotheses, and developed proofs of concept and exploit stages, he said. Meanwhile, the AI pen-testing security startup’s researchers chose targets, provided context, challenged the agents’ results, and decided which attack components to chain. "We did apply a fair bit of our own human expertise and judgment," he wrote. Crossing two security boundaries in 3 steps Google’s Chrome browser uses several layers of security to protect users, and this includes sandboxes - barriers to contain compromised code and ensure that someone who hacks an individual website can’t take over the entire computer. This includes deploying the V8 sandbox to prevent any memory corruption flaws in the V8 JavaScript engine from impacting other memory. The V8 sandbox sits inside the operating-system process sandbox, and this nested design means that escaping V8's memory restrictions doesn't automatically grant native code execution. Even if an attacker achieves native code execution inside Chrome's renderer, the outer process sandbox restricts access to the rest of the machine. “The chain crossed both boundaries in three vulnerability stages,” abusing Chrome to run code on Windows machines, Dolan-Gavitt wrote. The attack combines a V8 compiler bug, an animated-WebP decoder bug, and a memory-safety bug in Crashpad. The first vulnerability is in Maglev, V8's mid-tier optimizing compiler, and it’s due to a reused, mutable boxed number during deoptimization. This gives attackers read and write access throughout V8's pointer-compression cage. The second stage, the animated-WebP bug, is a V8 sandbox escape. “But rather than attacking the sandbox itself we exploited a property that the V8 sandbox deliberately does not enforce and that Blink incorrectly assumed it could trust,” Dolan-Gavitt explained. “Finally, the exploit used an overflow in Crashpad to cross the final outer process boundary and achieve unsandboxed code execution on the host.” While Google patched all three security issues, and Chrome installs updates on its own, a fix only takes effect once the user relaunches the browser. If you use Chrome, make sure you are running version 152.0.7977.82 or later. The time and money spent to achieve a full chain Chrome exploit illustrate - yet again - that “the bar is significantly lower” for attackers armed with LLMs, Dolan-Gavitt wrote. “Defend accordingly.”®

7d1817243c7da73d: Environmentalists of all political hues must find the language and ideas that turn passion for climate action into impetus The future of Green politics is under constant discussion after the Holborn and St Pancras byelection, but a much heavier clash – in meaning, symbolism and portent – happened earlier this summer, in King’s Lynn and West Norfolk. 9fae150173d88ae1: Ivanti customers are being urged to update Connect Secure and check for compromise after attackers exploited a newly disclosed zero-day vulnerability. Rated 8.6 on the CVSS scale, it allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands. "We are aware of exploitation in the wild affecting a limited number of customers at the time of disclosure," the vendor said in its advisory. There are limited indicators of compromise available at present, it said, advising customers to refer to Volexity's report on the findings for more information, and to run the Ivanti Integrity Checker Tool regularly. Ivanti lists affected releases in the following branches: 25.1.1.1 and earlier 25.1.2.2 and earlier 22.8R2.4 and earlier The vendor said it previously identified "a portion of this vulnerability" and patched it in July's 25.1.3.0 update, and had been working on backporting the same fix since then, however, attackers began exploiting it before that work was complete. Volexity said the attackers behind the recent intrusions were previously unknown to its researchers, but are now tracked as UTA0576. Criminal motive rather than espionage is suspected by Volexity. Based on observed post-exploitation activity, attackers appeared to be most interested in using their newfound access for credential theft, data exfiltration, log tampering, and network reconnaissance. Notably, the attackers did not deploy any malware nor execute web shells, using only the commands available to them on the ICS appliance. "Because the operation was detected and disrupted, the threat actor's ultimate objectives could not be determined," said Volexity. "However, Volexity assesses with high confidence that UTA0576's actions signaled preparation for lateral movement and a broader compromise of the victim network." The researchers also suspect that the attackers were using large language models to support their endeavors. Volexity pointed to the attackers' repeated use of the exploit channel to run commands, rather than deploying web shells, and their use of "highly specific scripts using hardcoded credentials." Ivanti disclosed one CVE, but Volexity described an attack chain involving three vulnerabilities. Tuesday's updates address the authentication bypass and remote code execution stages. The third vulnerability, which allows privilege escalation, is separate from the flaws encompassed by CVE-2026-104935. Volexity said Ivanti is aware of the additional bug and plans to publish a fix "in the coming weeks." The disclosure of the zero-day this week makes it the third year running that Ivanti has had to deal with attackers exploiting undisclosed flaws in Connect Secure. The previous ICS zero-days were disclosed in January 2025, a year after the January 2024 vulnerabilities led to exploits affecting thousands of ICS appliances. In the interim, we've also seen suspected Chinese espionage groups exploiting bugs in Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM), and critical flaws in Sentry. Ivanti's run of January zero-days continued earlier this year, although those flaws affected EPMM rather than Connect Secure. ®
972ce96df38a5766: A protein is a chain of amino acids held together by what are called peptide bonds. On their own, those bonds are extremely stable; they're estimated to have a half-life of several hundred years. But in Earth's environment, most proteins don't last nearly that long. That's because organisms have evolved a handful of ways to catalyze the break-up of peptide bonds, which have diversified into countless specialized protein-digesting enzymes. Proteases are everywhere and generally make short work of any proteins that find their way into the environment.

Now, researchers have basically short-circuited the diversification process, using AI-based protein design tools to take the catalytic core of two types of protease and replace the entire rest of the protein. The resulting enzymes could be tuned to cut specific proteins in half, and the researchers demonstrated their effectiveness by using them to cut proteins associated with neurological diseases.

The basic peptide bond isn't especially interesting-looking—it's what you get when you link an amino group to an acid, releasing a water molecule in the process. As their name implies, amino acids have both an amino and an acid group, allowing them to form peptide bonds on two sides of the amino acid. This is critical for building up the long chains found in proteins. (The amino acids also have side chains with distinctive chemistry, which gives a backbone specific properties.)

ceb6a0020de2d9e5: It's about time: the General Conference on Weights and Measures looks set to end leap seconds in an effort to reach horological harmony. Since 1972, 27 leap seconds have been added to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to keep it in step with the astronomical time scale UT1, which is based on Earth's fluctuating rotation. The proposal would increase the permitted difference between UTC and UT1 from 0.9 seconds to one hour, avoiding leap-second adjustments for centuries. Earth's rotation has also sped up in recent years, raising the possibility of a negative leap second – removing a second rather than adding one. That has never been done before. Experts have estimated a 30 percent probability that global systems will need a negative leap second by 2035 to keep the two time measures in step. That could pose problems for computer systems designed to handle added seconds but not removed ones. Many national bodies support the proposal, which is expected to pass. If approved, the change would take effect on May 20, 2027. Setnam Shemar, principal scientist at the UK's National Physical Laboratory, said the proposal would avoid the risks associated with leap seconds for centuries. "Leap seconds can be difficult to implement reliably, and if not applied correctly, they can cause differences in time across networks, potentially leading to the failure of systems such as mobile phone networks or electricity grids. These risks could increase if a negative leap second had to be implemented for the first time. "Previously, leap seconds were added to UTC to keep it within 0.9 seconds of UT1. From 20 May 2027, a difference of up to 1 hour will be allowed before intervention is needed, ensuring the continuity of UTC for several centuries or more. "The relationship between UTC and UT1 is important for some applications, such as astronomy and celestial navigation. The decision would not sever that link: UT1 will continue to be monitored, and its difference from UTC will continue to be disseminated through established international services." ®
88d33e11bddc035f: Silicon Valley’s AI bros have supposedly found a new way to signal to those around them how committed they are to their industry: Take up smoking despite the risk of cancer, because they expect bots to develop a cure … any day now. At least, that’s the claim Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar made in a recent interview on CBS's Face the Nation. In trying to explain what he described as a doomsday cult surrounding effective altruism, whose adherents include some AI researchers who believe the technology could bring about a utopia, Sankar claimed smoking has become a way for researchers to demonstrate their faith in the tech. “So many AI researchers have started smoking as a way of signaling to other researchers how much they believe in AI,” Sankar said to the confusion of host Margaret Brennan. Those researchers “believe so much in AI that it's going to cure cancer, I'm showing you my chips are all in,” Sankar explained. Sankar described the decision to take up smoking as a bet that AI would cure any health ailments that arose from it as “mass psychosis” and “social delusion” that’s getting in the way of actual discussions around the state of AI, and he blamed Silicon Valley’s pet philosophy, effective altruism, for those delusions. “There's an unseen force driving the narrative around AI safety, and it's really this millenarian doomsday cult meets messianic complex called effective altruism,” Sankar said. That philosophy prioritizes making the most effective decisions that benefit the most humans – like utilitarianism on steroids – and it tends to take a long-term approach to things. That’s where AI comes in: Effective altruists are ostensibly focused on ensuring AI systems are built in a way that will best benefit humanity. That focus has been a key reason why so much AI doomerism has come out of Silicon Valley too: If we’re going to build safe AI, says the effective altruist, we have to make sure that we consider all the risks. “There's only really roughly 2,000 AI researchers in America, and the vast majority of them believe in this sort of worldview around effective altruism,” Sankar noted. The Palantir CTO seems to believe, like many effective altruism critics, that all the doomsday scenarios and far-fetched risks being posited by the EA AI crowd are less technical critiques and more like theological ones. “I think there's a profound truth to Pascal's saying that every human has a god-shaped hole in their heart,” Sankar said, “and it's important to understand that many of these folks in Silicon Valley who are building this technology have filled that hole with the machine God of AGI.” Smoking as a bet that the machine god will save them from cancer, therefore, is akin to the ascetic’s endurance of physical pain or trauma in the hopes God will heal them or see them safely through their torment. From a more practical perspective, this isn’t exactly a great idea, as one former cancer researcher who spoke to The Register told us. “Good luck to them with this approach,” the researcher, who declined to be named, opined. “Even more so, good luck to their non-smoking friends and family taking in their passive smoke.” Taking up smoking in the hopes of a cure may not be a wise idea when one considers the timeline needed to develop a cancer drug, much less a cancer cure. "Even with AI, developing and introducing a new cancer drug into any of the world's health systems can take several years,” the researcher explained. “Even then we wouldn't know whether or not resistance to the drug would develop in the tumors.” The ability of AI to discover drugs and medical treatments has been much hyped – Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis even predicted last year that 2025 would be the year humans started popping AI-designed pills. That hasn’t happened yet, and there’s no real indication it will anytime soon. In other words, the likelihood that AI is going to kill us all is ridiculously overblown. The actual casualties, it seems, are more likely to be the AI bros giving themselves cancer as a show of faith in their machine god. ®

339aa8baab926568: A browser-based emulator for the original iPhone is the latest project to tap into the rich vein of nostalgia running through the tech industry. While far from a complete implementation, the emulation does enough to evoke happier times, before Apple burdened its mobile operating system with frills and complexities, and spent years (and multiple operating system updates) making the Podcasts app steadily more broken. The browser-based emulation (and we use the term carefully; anyone expecting all the functionality of yesteryear will be sorely disappointed) shows an original iPhone as it debuted in 2007. The buttons are where you remember them, the screen is ringed by bezels that wouldn't pass muster today, and the skeuomorphic icons are all present and correct. There's even the browser, though it doesn't do much yet. Even a gentle prod shows how incomplete this implementation is. Some apps work well, such as Calculator, while others - Contacts - struggle, and anything that needs an online connection fails, including loading today's web in 2007's Safari. It does, however, recall how simple things were almost 20 years ago, when the iPhone first appeared, and it joins an array of old-time systems that can be fired up (or at least look like they are) in a browser. Want a look at Apple's abandoned System 7 replacement? Step this way. Perhaps an XP-like implementation? No problem. It would be churlish to dwell on the emulation's deficiencies. For now, it's arguably more curiosity than anything else: Apple didn't launch the App Store until 2008, so third-party apps would be off the table, at least until a later version of iOS landed. Running it in a browser is undoubtedly convenient, though. Alternatives such as Light Touch offer a fuller implementation, but they demand more than a handy Chrome instance on a Windows device to open a portal back to a brighter time. So, fire up 2006's Nintendo Wii, pop on that CD of Back to Black, and relive the excitement of switching on the very first iPhone. Although perhaps give that other 2007 icon, Windows Vista, a bit of a swerve… ®
a6948736316dfc23: Gigabyte recently announced new motherboards that use DDR4 RAM, a standard that launched in 2014, and other vendors support even older standards in brand-new kit. Earlier this year, AMD released a Ryzen 7 5800X3D anniversary edition to mark ten years of AM4. This is notable because of the age of the DDR4 spec. In case you lose track of these things, The Register first described the new DDR4 spec back in 2012, and a few months later urged the keen to wait a year or two. DDR5 supports higher transfer rates, and The Reg predicted its arrival in 2017. The DDR5 standard was agreed in 2020, with mainstream PC adoption following in 2021. Over in the People's Republic of China, several vendors will sell you new DDR3 motherboards for 15-year-old server CPUs, such as Huananzhi's X79-4D or X79 Supreme, or the Machinist X79 V2.82H.
